#3916. Former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect to curb AI clones

Former Rockstar Games North technical director Obbe Vermeij believes that the possibility of AI vibe coded ports of Grand Theft Auto 6 could push Rockstar to create an official PC version sooner than you'd expect.

Speaking to RockPaperShotgun as part of a wider interview, Vermeij said generative AI "really has changed the world.". He elaborated: "I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as [the developer's] effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together."

Vermeij emphasised that he doesn't know what Rockstar's plans are, but with his technical expertise, he does believe that generative AI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a GTA 6 PC port.

"It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things," Vermeij said. "And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it.".

We've already seen people thrust footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 into AI software over the past few months. AI slop videos have been pulling in millions of views on social media, and people have been 'improving' trailer footage with Nvidia's DLSS5 'yassification' machine (thanks Ars Technica). Grand Theft Auto 6 itself will not feature any generative AI or microtransactions at launch.

AI game clones continue to be a problem. Game developers have cancelled public demos in fear of having their game copied, and Steam owner Valve has gone out to say it's the developer's responsibility to prevent cloning by making their games more original. Even as Anthropic has introduced measures to prevent such practices, other AI software can still perform such tasks.

The Legend of Zelda might be one of Nintendo's biggest series, but according to two of the company's former marketing leads, it was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild, which introduced a massive open-world overhaul that left the franchise's classic formula behind.

Last week saw the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake, which is already an enormous success with 5.2 million copies sold in its first four days. Notably, although it's a remake rather than an entirely new game, it shows there's still a huge appetite for the classic Zelda formula – something that Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang have been discussing in a new episode of their podcast below.

Ellis and Yang – former director of social media marketing and original content, and senior manager of creator relations and original content at Nintendo of America, respectively – have been chatting about whether the Ocarina of Time remake could open the door for more traditional Zelda games going forward, as opposed to the Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom-style open-world games which have served as the series' most major releases in the last nine years. While Yang would be interested in a game that combines the classic Zelda-style dungeons with the open-world format, Ellis would "like to see a modern attempt on a classic Zelda game" with that aspect left out entirely.

However, this brings him to another point – what he calls "revisionist history" of the series' releases. He calls out fans who've suggested that "the Zelda team ripped these [classic-style games] away from us at the peak of their popularity," prompting Yang to jump in: "That's ridiculous. This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing."

Ellis recalls: "I remember, I was going to the focus groups. It was a really dark moment of like, the feedback is 'the fan base is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players.'" According to him, Nintendo had "so much data" showing that "the interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with every new game. As a result, he says, "They had to do something dramatic like that."

Obviously, Breath of the Wild was an enormous success – per Nintendo's data, as of the end of September, the Switch 1 version had sold a whopping 34.28 million copies, with its sequel Tears of the Kingdom coming in with 22.9 million. They're both considered some of the best Zelda games of all time, and for good reason.

But, as Ellis and Yang discuss, the Ocarina of Time remake has already proven that folks enjoy the more traditional experiences, too. I don't think we were ever at risk of Zelda going totally open world – even since Breath of the Wild's launch, we've seen the Link's Awakening remake and Echoes of Wisdom, as well as Skyward Sword's HD remaster, giving us new top-down and 3D releases, respectively.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

Like Ellis, though, I'd be keen to see a brand new, classic-style 3D Zelda game at some point. After all, not counting remakes, remasters, and ports, the last one was technically 2011's Skyward Sword – it's fair to say we're due for something fresh.

Despite GTA 6 being pitted against Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Take-Two boss has nothing but praise – Nintendo "should be proud" as the game is "terrific."

I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite.

#3913. Cyberattack on Sega third-party newsletter distributor reportedly sees over two million email addresses leaked, but Sega accounts unaffected

Japanese email distribution firm Arara were the target of the attack

Sega have revealed that over two million email addresses have leaked due to a cyberattack on Japanese email delivery provider Arara, whom the Like A Dragon and Sonic publishers use to distribute newsletters. Sega and Arara are currently busy investigating what happened in the breach, which doesn't appear to have affected the Sega accounts you can use receive in-game rewards and access a calendar which reminds you when it's Kazuma Kiryu's birthday. The companies have urged those who signed up for the affected newsletters to be wary of potential phishing attempts.

According to Automaton, who've translated Sega's official press release about the cyberattack, 2,196,044 email addresses in total were affected. 92,273 of that number were linked to the newsletter distribution.

The company have listed some specific newsletter releases as having been affected, including two exhibition announcements for this year's Tokyo Game Show, the announcement of arcade rhythm game Chunithm Mate's launch, six newsletters about online character lottery service Sega Lucky Kuji Online, the launch of a rhythm game update dubbed Ongeki Re:Fresh Act.2, and the launch of another arcade rhythm game update called Maimai DX MAGiCAL. Number one, that's a lot of rhythm games, and number two, Sega have advised those who opted in and received those newsletters to watch out for fishing emails from people posing as being tied to Sega or Arara.

Sega reportedly confirmed that - as far as the affected emails go - no names, dates of birth, genders, residential addresses, phone numbers, credit card information, and passwords are known to have been leaked. There had also been no reports of cases where the leaked information had been misused as of the time Sega made their announcement. The company have naturally put distributing any further email newsletters through Arara on hold until their investigation's done and plan to reach out to each affected person individually once the full details of the leak have been confirmed.

While data breaches and cyberattacks are nothing new, there have been a fair few recently, with both Street Fighter makers Capcom and Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 devs Warhorse suffering incidents of their own last month.

#3912. Following BioWare's shock closure, a new documentary capturing its final moments is coming next year

A documentary detailing the history of beloved Mass Effect studio BioWare is releasing next year, and will cover last month's shock closure of the studio, following the private acquisition of owner EA.

Mass Effect: The BioWare Story (per Deadline) has been written and directed by Akash Sherman and produced for Canada's Super Channel. It documents the studio from the early days after its founding in 1995 to the release of barn-burner hits like Mass Effect and Dragon Age. Filming began two years prior to the announcement of BioWare's closure and continued throughout, with Deadline reporting the documentary will "capture BioWare’s final chapter."

The BioWare Story includes interviews with studio founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, alongside Mass Effect director Casey Hudson, other BioWare developers, and Shepard voice actor Jennifer Hale. That's alongside former EA CEO John Riccitiello, LucasFilm Games vice president Douglas Reilly, and creator of The Game Awards Geoff Keighley.

"The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” writer and director Sherman said in a statement accompanying the documentary news. "It's a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction."

For fans outside Canada, Mass Effect: The BioWare Story is planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere next year. No exact release date has been established as of writing.

Members of the games industry have lambasted EA's decision to close Bioware in the weeks since the news was shared, with legendary designer Warren Spector writing, "Anyone who participated in this travesty should be ashamed". Meanwhile, a petition has reached enough signatures for the Canadian government to potentially rescue the studio from closure. Whether or not it actually does… Well, weirder things have happened?

Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as Nvidia CEO. That's such an odd sentence to write, as a huge part of my career as a tech journalist has revolved around covering Nvidia, its graphics cards, and its leather-jacketed chief.

As I write this article, I'm already seeing reactions on social media from PC gamers. Some are shocked, some are indifferent, and some appear to be celebrating. In terms of the latter, I'd imagine that's because the ex-Nvidia boss has become one of the most recognisable figures behind the great AI revolution, which, err, isn't popular within our hobby, to say the least.

Not only that, but RAM is ludicrously expensive, with storage not far behind. And graphics cards, Nvidia's gaming bread and butter? The price increases recently have been mind-boggling. All of these things are, in the main, AI server-demand induced, and Nvidia is behind the chips that power most of those servers, making vast amounts of money in the process.

And so on that level, I can understand why some might cheer his departure, equating the company's figurehead with Nvidia's new place in the AI economy as a whole—leaving us gamers in the lurch. But as far as I see it, Jensen Huang leaving the helm of Nvidia is unlikely to be a good thing for PC gaming.

I'll give you an unfortunate percentage: 7.4%. That's roughly how much of Nvidia's total revenue was brought in by gaming in the 2026 fiscal year. The company reported $193.7 billion in data center revenue. Its gaming division? $16 billion. That's despite the fact the company is estimated to hold 90% of the PC graphics card market share.

In terms of business fundamentals, Nvidia would be foolish to put more focus on gaming hardware while the AI cash cow continues to provide. Huang, however, still seemed reluctant to leave PC gaming entirely by the wayside during his tenure.

Those who have watched as many Nvidia GPU announcements as I have will know that walking on stage with a new graphics card, or gaming laptop, lit up Huang's face the most. 3D graphics was where the company began, after all, back when founders Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem sat down at a Denny's in San Jose and put together a business plan. Or so the story goes.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

But now, someone new will be steering the ship. Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer will serve as interim CEO, while the search begins for Huang's permanent replacement.

Whoever they are, they'll be taking over an absolute titan of tech, the behemoth standing behind the US position in the great AI race, and a company that will need to convince its investors that the AI good times are far from over. How big a factor do you think consumer graphics cards are likely to be in those discussions?

Personally, I reckon they're going to be pretty far down the list of priorities. Because this is big business, money talks, and AI data centers are where most of the cash still lies. I wish that wasn't true, but the figures speak for themselves.

So, if Nvidia pivots even further away from gaming hardware, where might your next graphics card come from? There's always AMD, who's CEO has recently proudly declared it as "a data center-first company." Hmm, I'm not too confident on the focus there, either. Or Intel, which... oh jeez, you too?

I'm not saying consumer gaming hardware, or Nvidia graphics cards, are going to disappear entirely in the face of the AI onslaught. But what I am saying is that, love him or loathe him, Jensen Huang was still an advocate for PC gaming—at least out of sentimentality, if nothing else.

He who became one of the primary movers of the AI market now threatening our hobby, was also an integral part of PC gaming's success. But now, Nvidia is likely to be making some big changes, sans Huang—and I find it hard to believe that many of them will be in our favour.

3. Best mid-range: Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB

You name it, if it's PC gaming hardware he'll write words about it, with opinions and everything.

#3910. Swarmbreaker is an uncommonly mesmerising tower defence game in which enemies "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid"

It is said that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

In Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!"

"SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

#3909. Square Enix accidentally botches a Nier: Automata update, balloons required file size from 50GB to 366GB on PC

"Do you think games are silly little things?"

Yesterday, Nier: Automata received a new patch on Steam, adding more language support to the title - it can now be played with Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese options - but this new update also, somehow, inflated the file size of the game on PC from about 50GB to 366GB. D'oh! What's worse is, the update is not optional.

The cause of this, reportedly, is a bug that caused all the DLC in the YoRHa Edition of the game to become the same size as the base game - and the new download stacks them all concurrently. "Only SquareEnix can turn 40GB into 366GB with 8GB patch," says one dissatisfied Steam reviewer.

If you don't have space for this massive new file on your PC (and I can't say I blame you, it's ridiculous), there is a workaround, as confirmed by Square Enix in a tweet via its Japanese Twitter account.

"We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest update to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected," noted the publisher. "We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC."

It's quite ironic, really, that so many Steam reviewers are complaining about things like "I just need to delete 90% of my computer to install this" when a large part of the game is managing the software/programmes installed on your android protagonists in order to upgrade your abilities and stats. There's even an ending for uninstalling your OS on your mechanical main characters. I'd be inclined to suggest this is some sort of meta psy-op from creator Yoko Taro, but… nah, that's just fantasy, isn't it? Isn't it?

Speaking of Taro, earlier this year we learned that "Nier Automata will continue", though we only heard back in 2025 that most of the projects the developer was working on were cancelled. One of these may have been the Tencent-backed Nier mobile game in 2024, which reportedly "struggled to find a monetisation to offset its high costs."

A Link Between Worlds is on Switch Online, apparently... or at least, Nintendo seems to think so

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

An official The Legend of Zelda website has listed the 3DS title A Link Between Worlds as available on Nintendo Switch Online, leading to speculation that the handheld's library could be coming to the service.

The Legend of Zelda fans are in a pretty good place when it comes to the series on Switch. If you have a Switch 2, you have access to every mainline entry in the series barring Four Swords Adventures, Twilight Princess, Phantom Hourglass, Spirit Tracks, A Link Between Worlds, and the somehow considered mainline Tri Force Heroes. And while Four Swords Adventures and Twilight Princess are on the cards thanks to the GameCube Nintendo Switch Online app, the handheld titles are generally seen as unlikely due to their dual screens.

However, on the Zelda Game History page on the Nintendo website, some have noticed an interesting disclaimer. You can click on each game to see a blurb about it, and with the games that are available to play on Nintendo Switch Online, there's a little mark showing this. Naturally this is present on the original NES game, Ocarina of Time, Wind Waker and the like, however, it's also present on The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds for the 3DS.

Obviously, there currently isn't a 3DS app available on Switch or Switch 2, and in theory, next in line would be the Wii, DS, and 3DS before we reach the Wii U – which already has all of its major titles on Switch – and then the Switch era itself. Theoretically, A Link Between Worlds would be easier to make work than the DS duology due to the second screen effectively being a menu screen.

However, I'm not sure I'd get my hopes up. Firstly, if the Game Boy Advance is exclusive to Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack users, there's no way that the 3DS would be on the regular Nintendo Switch Online subscription. And as a user on Reddit points out, The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages – which is already on Switch Online and specifically as part of the non-Expansion Pack subscription – is missing its "Playable with Nintendo Switch Online" label, so it's likely somehow been mixed up with A Link Between Worlds.

That being said, it does hammer home that Nintendo is currently letting one of the best Legend of Zelda games of all-time remain unplayable on modern hardware since the 3DS store was discontinued, so a 3DS Nintendo Switch Online would be appreciated, as many of the other comments on Reddit prove.

#3906. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy releases in January, leaving not very long to prepare for all the crunchy cRPG choices and secret wars it'll lob your way

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the not so far away future

Oh shit, that's not too far away. Terrifyingly, that last sentence is now a thing I can accurately write about games coming out in January 2027. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy has just been confirmed as one such game, with the cRPG's heresy investigation set to commence towards the end of the month.

January 28th, 2027, is the full Dark Heresy release date, as announced by devs Owlcat on Steam. The beta version of the game'll be closing down on January 7th to make way for the full game, so as of writing there's still some time to give that a go if you fancy.

If this is the first you've heard of Dark Heresy, here's Owlcat's synopsis of what it's all about:

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the far future in a cRPG set in the rich Warhammer 40,000 universe. Start your service as an acolyte of the Inquisition: Investigate heresy, command a diverse warband, and shape the fate of the Calixis Sector in a story-rich experience where every decision has weight, justice is non-existent, and the line between salvation and damnation is razor-thin. Explore an in-depth depiction of the Inquisition as an organisation and the vast force it commands: its power, bureaucracy, and inner conflicts laid bare like never before.

As an Inquisitor, you have one primary goal: to protect the Imperium, whether that be from the taint of xenos, the betrayal of heretics, or the scourge of mutants, by any means necessary. Be the conduit of the Emperor’s will in a place where all hope was lost decades ago, explore the mysteries of the maddening Tyrant Star, and overcome the worst horrors thrown at you by the Noctis Aeterna.

A place where all hope was lost decades ago? You sure this is the Warhammerverse and not real life lads? I jest, but bursting into rooms and shouting 'Nobody expects the God-Emperor’s inquisition!' Monty Python-style does sound quite fun. Oisin's previously written in more depth about what Dark Heresy devs have said regarding what to expect from its investigations, if you want nitty-gritty details rather than references to sketch comedy.

If you're so inclined, Dark Heresy is wishlistable on Steam.

#3905. World of Warcraft: Forever hotfix puts a stop to super speedy flag carriers that were dominating PvP battlegrounds

World of Warcraft: Forever has received its first major hotfix patch, which among other things has put an end to an especially powerful bug that made PvP battlegrounds like Warsong Gulch favoured to the Horde's advantage.

While Taurens are running, they gradually build up stacks of increased movement speed. They gain a two percent movement speed bonus per stack, and it stacks up to 30 times. That means a Tauren can gain 60 percent increased movement speed, though it's worth noting that when they stop moving, these stacks decrease. In short, cows run fast.

The Hotfix, detailed in this Blizzard blog post, stops the Tauren's plainsrunning passive from stacking during a battleground's preparation phase. What players were doing to exploit this was running back and forth in the minutes before the Warsong Gulch battleground let both teams loose. It's a capture the flag game mode, so once the gates opened, Taurens were sprinting ahead of everyone else, allowing them to quickly push towards the enemy base for a potential early flag capture.

In addition, the hotfix removes any plainsrunning stacks from Taurens once they pick up the enemy flag, and prevents them from gaining stacks while the flag is in their possession. The goal of the enemy team is to stop and kill the enemy flag carrier as soon as possible, so a Tauren moving far faster than any of your team made this pretty difficult.

Tauren's could be tanky warriors or druids too, which further added to the difficulty in killing them. With this change they're now easier to lock down, though it's worth noting a Tauren can still make use of Plainsrunning to rush into the enemy base early. They just don't have that wild speed boost from the jump.

Surely this was the only reason my Alliance Warsong Gulch games were all lost this morning, and not because my faction is for chumps. In other World of Warcraft: Forever news, the launch earlier this week was applauded as one of the smoothest in the series history, save for a few broken boats and zeppelins.

The hotfix has also decreased the respawn time of the NPC Deathstalker Erland who is needed for an escort quest. People were mulling around his spawn and wasting away while waiting for him to respawn. Also, supply vendors on the Zephras Isle have been stocked with handy tradeskill bags that you could find in other starter zones. It's the shipping I assume, it takes a while for stock to make it all the way up there.

There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great.November 11, 2026

We thought it might be coming, and it's here: Jensen Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia, as he has resigned following an admitted affair, and an additional alleged one.

It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. And, well, there's certainly some truth in that given we saw company share prices drop after reports of Huang's alleged second affair came to light.

After perusing X for a while today, the general sentiment seems to be that Huang was so incredibly central to Nvidia that the company couldn't possibly do well without him. Or at the very least, nowhere near as well as it would with Jensen sticking at the helm. Ditto the AI market in general.

But not everyone agrees. In fact, one of the most credible voices on Nvidia reckons there are "strong" and "excellent" candidates for a replacement. Tae Kim wrote the most well-known, authoritative book on the company—The Nvidia Way—and yesterday they explained:

"Many people have cited my book as saying Nvidia would be completely lost without Jensen Huang. My views have evolved in the several years since I wrote those passages. I now believe there is a strong internal candidate with the technical expertise, experience, customer relationships and respect of employees needed to lead Nvidia effectively into its next chapter."

"There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great."

They're certainly optimistic comments, but your guess is as good as mine as to who they might be referring to—presumably someone on the list of potential replacement CEO candidates I put together earlier.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

We now know that the actual interim CEO is Colette Kress—exactly who we predicted it would be. I'm not sure whether that's who Kim had in mind, given they decided, for some strange reason, to not mention who they were thinking of by name. But if not, there's still room for the next proper CEO to be one of those he has in mind.

This being said, Jensen Huang's status, drive, and deep familiarity with the company and the market are undoubtedly unparalleled. I think you'd find it difficult to pin down anyone who could reasonably disagree with that. In which case, while Nvidia might not be "completely lost", it's hard to say it will be as oriented as it would be with Huang still at the helm.

#3903. Strategy RPG Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds coming to PS5 in May 2027

Ontario-based developer Ocelot Technologies will release strategy RPG Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds for PlayStation 5 alongside its full release for PC via Steam in May 2027, the developer announced.

Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds first launched in Early Access for PC on October 10, 2024.

“We’ve been very happy with how much our audience has embraced Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds throughout its Early Access era, but we’ve always dreamt of bringing it to consoles, where our love of the genre first began,” said Ocelot Technologies CEO Mike in a press release. “PlayStation is the perfect place for Guild Saga, as we were massively inspired by the JRPGs that have long made PlayStation such a titan in the industry. Having it available on [PlayStation 5] feels like a homecoming, so we can’t wait for PlayStation fans to set sail to the Respite Archipelago in May!”

Here is an overview of the game, via lead developer Yasser Saleem on PlayStation Blog:

Create your hero’s appearance and choose their background, talents, and skills.

We wanted character building to leave room for creativity and experimentation. The progression system lets you combine skills across disciplines freely, as opposed to a more rigid class system. Skills let you deal damage, heal allies, change the environment, reposition across the battlefield, summon creatures, and alter the turn sequence. With hundreds of items, you can shape both your character’s build and their appearance, choosing gear that suits your playstyle and the look you want.

Your companions offer more opportunities to shape the party. Each brings a distinct history and personal quests, while their equipment, abilities, and attributes can be completely customized.

Through dialogue and shared experiences, you’ll discover more about the companions you choose to bring along. Friendships and romance can become part of your journey, giving you connections to your party members beyond the battlefield.

Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds features tactical turn-based combat with approximately 200 skills across ten disciplines. Express your tactical creativity by exploring how skills across different schools work together and with the environment around you.

Surface interactions and weather are an important consideration in combat. Players will need to be mindful of how surfaces interact, how weather affects the battle, and how those conditions might alter their skills.

For example, a party member with points invested in Geomancer may summon a mandrake to join the fight. A companion with Hydromancer skills can then make it rain, watering the mandrake and causing it to grow into a more formidable force. A party member with Aeromancer skills may then use lightning to electrify the puddles, paralyzing anyone standing in them. Across three disciplines, you’ve summoned an ally, strengthened it through the weather, and turned the resulting surfaces into a tactical advantage. We want players to discover combinations like this and experiment with how their party’s abilities work together.

Preparation matters too. Looting, mining, and gathering herbs provide materials you can craft into weapons, equipment, arrows, potions, and food. Whether you’re replenishing supplies or crafting new gear for a companion, taking time to explore and gather resources can help your party prepare for the next battle.

When designing exploration, we wanted players to feel that taking their time could lead to something worth finding. The main quest gives your journey direction, but the islands also invite you to wander, speak to NPCs, and investigate what catches your attention.

You might find yourself solving a murder mystery, hunting feared monsters for bounty money, or settling a deadly dispute between farm animals. Elsewhere, you can follow the imagination of a famed explorer or uncover an alchemical conspiracy. These side quests give you reasons to get to know the archipelago’s inhabitants and become involved in their troubles, whether sinister, strange, or absurd.

We wanted that variety to make following a new lead feel exciting. A conversation that seems like a small diversion can draw you into a story with its own characters, conflicts, and discoveries. Taking a detour is an opportunity to experience another side of the world and the people inhabiting it.

Hidden treasures, puzzles, valuable crafting resources, and unexpected encounters also reward exploration. Ancient books and forgotten notes offer glimpses into the world’s past, giving curious players more to uncover along the way.

We’re looking forward to welcoming PlayStation players into Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds when it launches on PlayStation 5 in May 2027. We’ll share the exact release date closer to launch.

#3902. Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

So long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the big national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have plans for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Currently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the big money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

The next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

Except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

#3901. Bringing Bloodborne back is tricky because "there's a lot of involved rights associated," according to former PlayStation boss

Every year, Bloodborne fans pray for the birth of another game set in FromSoftware's Lovecraftian world. Every year, we're no closer to a Bloodborne 2 or even a Bloodborne Remastered. But why? PlayStation's former head honcho, Shawn Layden, blames it on the tricky situation of rights ownership.

Asked about the noticeable lack of Bloodborne in the decade since its blood moon shone down on us all, in an interview with The Trophy Room podcast, Layden explained that returning to any beloved game is tough.

"Bringing back old games has a certain challenge to it," he said. "Can you do something that is not only respectful of the original, but can you, you know, recreate the phenomenon as it were?"

Bloodborne's situation is slightly more complicated, though. It seems that the rights are somehow split between original publisher PlayStation, developer FromSoftware and the studio's primary stakeholder Kadokawa Corporation.

"There's a lot of involved rights associated with it, and in something like that - where Sony's in there and [FromSoftware] is in there and From's parent company is in there - I think just getting everyone to sign off on the same thing is probably the biggest challenge there," Layden said.

Having led the PlayStation brand during most of its PS4 golden years, Layden said working with FromSoftware on Bloodborne and the original Demon's Souls was "fantastic."

Despite endless calls for a comeback and very stable sales more than a decade on, Bloodborne itself is still stuck on the PS4 - though it's still playable via backward compatibility on the PS5, I should add. The closest we seemingly got to a Bloodborne comeback came from Bluepoint Games, which reportedly pitched a remake sometime before parent company PlayStation shut down the acclaimed studio, though FromSoftware supposedly didn't want the project to go ahead.

Another former PlayStation executive, Shuhei Yoshida, previously speculated that Bloodborne hasn't been remade because game director and soulslike pioneer, Hidetaka Miyazaki, would prefer to handle it himself: "Miyazaki-san really, really loved Bloodborne, what he created… So I think he is interested but he's so successful and he's so busy, so he cannot do it himself, and he doesn't want anyone else to touch it."

Elsewhere, a Bloodborne animated feature is in the works with YouTuber JackSepticEye attached as a co-producer.

#3899. Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

So, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest."

If I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Big Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together."

#3898. Mass Effect-like RPG The Expanse: Osiris Reborn ropes in David Gaider, the original lead writer of Bioware's Dragon Age series

"Focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative."

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn looks like it's carrying the best bits of Mass Effect forward, and in an encouraging move, the developers have been collaborating with David Gaider.

Of course, David Gaider is best known as the lead writer on Dragon Age: Origins, Dragon Age 2 and Dragon Age: Inquisition - he's also often credited as the architect of its dark fantasy world Thedas. Gaider's post-BioWare career saw him open his own game development house Summerfall Studios, which most recently released an ambitious roleplaying musical called Stray Gods.

But he's now lending a hand to a game that's not too dissimilar to BioWare's other hugely famous roleplaying series, while still working on his own games at Summerfall.

"Alongside my work at Summerfall, I've also been collaborating with the Owlcat Games team on The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative. The Expanse has long been one of my favourite series, and so obviously I jumped at the opportunity to be involved," he wrote on BlueSky.

"The Owlcat team has been so great, it's really such a treat. One thing I enjoy is how responsive they are to the fans," Gaider added, pointing to how the studio recently recast the male version of its protagonist in response to feedback. The game's reworked and re-designed Martian Captain is now voiced by Blythe Melin.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn shouldn't be confused for the other very Mass Effect-y RPG coming out next year, Exodus. Though it's good to hear that both upcoming projects have some BioWare veterans on board, especially after the famed developer was shut down and had its own promising, actual Mass Effect game cancelled.

Bertie enjoyed what he played of the upcoming game in Eurogamer's The Expanse preview, but also had some concerns about the developer's use of generative AI.

#3895. Updated Xbox PC app promises 60% faster loading and easier access to games, but CEO Asha Sharma says there's "plenty more to do"

The Xbox PC app hasn't had the best track record in recent years, but Microsoft is promising that it's now much faster and easier to use than before.

Starting today, anyone part of the Xbox Insiders program can try out the new improvements. According to Microsoft, the updated Xbox PC app now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50% faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65% faster. The company acknowledged that performance can vary based on your set up, internet connection, device, and so on.

The rest of the update involves "simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organise your games," according to Xbox Wire, while social features are now included in the main navigation menu so you can start playing or chatting with friends quicker.

A faster Xbox PC app is certainly nice for players who regularly use it, though it's still missing a lot of the features that make Steam the go-to place to buy PC games. CEO Asha Sharma called the update "a meaningful improvement," but acknowledged there's still "plenty more to do."

Microsoft also said "it's easier to find what you're looking for" using the app's search function, and refreshed game cards and animations should give the platform "a cleaner look and feel."

Elsewhere, the revamped cloud gaming setup will roll out to even more people using web browsers, and more Xbox Insiders should hear about the program over the next few weeks. "The updated experience also makes it easier to find and play your games," the company said while bringing attention to its new light and dark modes. Supported smart TVs and VR headsets will get the updated cloud experience, as well.

Earlier this year, the console maker brought a selection of 'classic' games to PC for the first time ever - Blinx: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge and Fuzion Frenzy led the first batch. Mythic Achievements - the Platinum Trophy equivalent - went live for all Xbox players, too.

#3894. Lucky Luke: The Lonesome Cowboy Collection announced for PS5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC

Atari publishing label Infogrames and developers Graphite Lab and Implicit Conversions have announced Lucky Luke: The Lonesome Cowboy Collection, a collection of seven Lucky Luke games from Game Boy Color, Super Nintendo Entertainment System, PlayStation, and Game Boy Advance. It will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC via Steam on January 13, 2027.

Here is an overview of the collection, via Infogrames.

Lucky Luke: The Lonesome Cowboy Collection brings seven Lucky Luke titles from the 8-, 16-, and 32-bit eras to all modern platforms for the first time.

Lucky Luke: The Lonesome Cowboy Collection includes

Every game features quality-of-life improvements, including improved graphics, save states, achievements, visual filters, custom screen bezels, and rebindable controls. “How to Play” guides onboard unfamiliar players and help them solve difficult challenges.

The bonus Frontier Experience is an interactive first-person museum and shooting gallery that allows players to explore the history of the iconic gunslinger firsthand. Players can explore western locales, enjoy target-shooting minigames, search for collectibles and discover original comic and character art.

The legendary Lucky Luke originated in 1946 with a French-Belgian comic book about a street-smart gunslinger famous for shooting faster than his own shadow. Over the past 70 years the cowboy has gone on to feature in numerous comics, several animated television series, feature films, and most recently a 2026 live-action television series.

The Lonesome Cowboy Collection reunites Infogrames with the popular western franchise. Infogrames published several Lucky Luke titles in the late 90s and early 2000’s, including the incredibly rare Playstation Platinum edition of Lucky Luke: Western Fever.

The collection includes four games that were only released here in Europe and never made it to the United States, including the 1997 Super Nintendo Entertainment System release of Lucky Luke, the 2000 Game Boy Color release of Lucky Luke: Desperado Train, the 2001 PlayStation release of Lucky Luke: Western Fever, and the 2001 Game Boy Advance release of Lucky Luke: Wanted!

#3893. Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the new mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

It's a "stopgap solution" while the site's staff are busy "working on more sophisticated tools"

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon."

Cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is important for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the issue for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected."

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

Personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

The finale of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy dares to expand even further from its world to character customization

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you thought Final Fantasy 7 Revelation was going to rein things in after the maximalist scale of Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, then think again. This is, after all, the finale of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy, so it's got to go out with a bang. Square Enix has also, so far, designed each instalment to be its own standalone RPG with a raft of new gameplay features rather than just a mere iteration of the next episode of the story.

While Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is already confirmed to be the largest entry to date – literally so with a file size estimated to be up to 200GB – there's plenty of new features that make this stand out from the already colossal achievements of its predecessors. This may still be a single-player story-driven party-based action RPG set over a planet-sized open world, but the developers have cooked up a lot more that demonstrates why it wasn't just called Final Fantasy 7 Remake Part 3.

There's potentially still more that Square Enix will reveal as the finale's April 8 launch date approaches, but from our hands-on time and official announcements made so far, these are the eight new features coming to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation that we feel is going to make this the most definitive of all the remake releases to date.

With the remake trilogy drawing to a close early 2027, we get ready for the epic conclusion with our Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Big Preview across hands-on impressions, dev access, and deep dives into the whole adventure so far.

Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth had already given us the impossible with an open world that really does encompass a world, and while Final Fantasy 7 Revelation adds to that with still several more locations, including Mideel and Wutai, its planetary scale has been magnified with verticality. You're not just fast-traveling to locations, but you have Cid's airship, the Highwind, which you can use to fly over any location and then jump out and parachute down seamlessly in real-time.

It's already a huge change from the original game where you could only access part of the overworld if you had enough space to land the Highwind. Instead of just warping to a set checkpoint, it also means if there's a nearby side quest marker, you can glide that way directly, or there might be another secret at a higher elevation you hadn't noticed before that's worth trying to land at to investigate. It's certainly a way to make revisiting places feel fresh again in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

While Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth had a new chocobo for each region, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation reunites you with yellow-feathered chocobo Piko from the Grasslands, this time as your sole mount. That might sound like something this instalment is reining in, but what it actually means is Piko will feel like a permanent addition to the party. Not just a mount for getting you from A to B, they'll actually level up and can even fight alongside you in battle.

Old-school fans may lament that there won't be chocobo-breeding like the original game, but I think having Piko grow and unlock new abilities, both in terms of traversal and combat, during your journey makes for a more meaningful companion than any other gaming mount. It's not like The Witcher 3's Roach was ever useful in a fight.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

Although Cid Highwind and Vincent Valentine were introduced in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, they become fully playable party members in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. While it will be exciting getting to grips with Cid's dragoon-style fighting style or Vincent's Galian beast transformation, you'll also be able to select them or any of the other party members as the playable character during exploration.

Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth did also try to mix things up occasionally in dungeons where the party would get split up or put you in control of a certain character in story-specific missions. Nonetheless, this small but meaningful change means you can spend more time controlling your favorite character while out in the wider world. It also makes sense given the story will cover the section when central protagonist Cloud will be out of action. And if you play as Vincent, it might be the closest we'll get to a Dirge of Cerberus remaster – it could still happen, right?

Arguably the most significant new feature in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is the FITS (Function-Integrated Tactical Suitwear) system, which may also sound rather similar to Dresspheres for any Final Fantasy 10-2 fans. Essentially, you can give each party member new threads or armor that also give them new classes that recall classic Final Fantasy jobs, such as Knight, Black Mage, or Summoner.

There's real style to this too as each outfit is tailored to each character rather than wearing the same job uniform. The abilities that come with each outfit are also actually additions rather than changing your class entirely, so if Tifa is dressed as a white mage, rest assured you can still kick ass with her divekick as before. That also means, if you're not looking to think too deeply about builds and just like the outfits as a cosmetic, then that's totally viable too.

The Black Materia is going to be a crucial plot point in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, as it's what allows Sephiroth to summon Meteor, and its ominous presence in the sky is going to be inescapable as you play through the game. Its activation will however also cause significant change to the world, notably the emergence of Weapons roaming the world.

Perhaps more significant is how the effects of Black Materia may alter the world's terrain. We can only speculate at this point what that can mean, but taking the addition of the Highwind and Piko into account as new ways of traversal, don't be surprised if the Grasslands suddenly has new structures or a rupture in the ground that require more verticality in traversal to explore. Call it the Tears of the Kingdom effect, but it should also mean you aren't just going back to explore the exact same regions as you left them in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth.

Equipping Materia to use spells or gain buffs remains a key aspect of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, though being treated as its own standalone game, I won't be surprised if that means having to upgrade them and find new Materia again, even if you might start with a default number of them as with Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth.

But, one area this finale plans to go further is how many Materia you can potentially link together. While we have already had gear that could link two Materia together, there may also be armor that can link three Materia together. That could mean being able to Magnify Materia to two separate spells so that they both reap the benefits, or potentially other uses that I'm still racking my brain over.

Synergy was a cool feature introduced in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth where you can have two party members team up together in battle. These ranged from real-time Synergy Skills like Aerith calling another party member to be her bodyguard or Tifa getting someone to launch her towards an enemy, to Synergy Abilities as show-stopping as Limit Breaks. How do you top that? Triple Synergy!

Given the three-person party size that was also true of the original game, it seems such a logical conclusion to have them all unite in one killer combo. That said, given the complexity of coordinating three characters simultaneously, I suspect this may just be limited to an ultimate ability that may only be available in specific situations, but expect them to leave a lasting impression.

Players looking for a proper challenge in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation don't need to finish the game to unlock a hard mode. Given how long this finale is going to be, that's already a tall order. But it also doesn't mean it's going to be hard mode available from the start but with that mode's item restrictions or enemies with double the health as with past games.

What it actually means in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is that because of the huge amount of side quests available and freedom to explore from very early on, there is absolutely nothing stopping you from taking on the toughest side quests and bosses even if you've vastly underleveled, while there are of course also the Weapons roaming the land, just tempting you to go pick a fight, whether or not you're ready.

#3891. Xbox is testing a way to use your phone as a controller on smart TVs

Xbox is testing two new ways to play its cloud games, and one of them doesn't require a controller at all.

Announced on Xbox Wire on 4th November, the phone controller preview is rolling out on supported TVs wherever Xbox Cloud Gaming is available. The phone option - which works with both Android and iOS devices - lets you use your phone "as a controller when you don't have one nearby". Connect to your TV via QR code, and the controls open in your phone's browser.

The second preview, called cloud connect, is currently limited to the US and lets the new Xbox Nano controller talk to your cloud session over wi- fi instead of pairing directly with your TV to "help reduce input latency, so gameplay feels more responsive".

To try out the phone controls yourself, switch on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest version of the Xbox smart TV app.

Xbox has published a setup guide with full instructions, although you should note that both experiences "are still being tested", so the availability and supported games or devices "may be limited while [Xbox] learns from your feedback".

ICYMI, as of yesterday, anyone in the Xbox Insider Program can try Microsoft's updated Xbox PC app. The company claims it now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50 percent faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65 percent faster.

The happiest time of year is just around the corner, folks. The PC Gaming Show: Most Wanted sponsored by Pot Noodle will be airing December 3rd, and we'll be counting down The Council's 20 most anticipated games.

There's one major change this year, though. We've gone from counting down the top 25 games to the top 20. We've made this decision to ensure each game gets its time in the spotlight, meaning the show will be more enjoyable to watch. Also, The Council have recently unionised and refuse to count more until we agree to give them bathroom breaks, which we simply will not do.

The Council remains, as ever, an inscrutable bunch of journalists, developers, celebrities, creators, streamers, gaming luminaries, and just generally people whose opinion on videogames carries some weight.

Each year, we knock our heads together and puzzle over how to whittle down the thousands of upcoming games into a list of just 100. Several factors go into this, such as how many wishlists a game has on Steam, how interesting a trailer is, the position of the stars at the time a game was first announced, and generally just how excited those of us at PC Gamer are for a title.

The full list awaits below, and the top 20 are nestled within it, but you'll never be able to figure out which ones they are. And if you do, please don't share your findings on the internet or you'll ruin the whole show. You'll notice there are fewer than 100 games, and that's because each year, some come out before the show or unfortunately get cancelled. Try as we might, we can't get The Council to predict the future—we'd all be retired by now if they could.

The Council gives each game they're excited for a score from one to five, with one being passingly curious to five being intensely, worryingly hyped. If a member has no interest in a game at all, they simply don't vote on it and that is counted as a zero.

We also take into account how many members of The Council voted for each game so that any with the same average score have a reliable tiebreaker. Some other factors go into the weighting, too, like if we've had no news about a game in a long time or, again, where the stars are and what they think of the whole thing.

#3889. Skydance Games lay off an undisclosed number of staff in the wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, in latest case of consolidation killing livelihoods

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

#3887. Wardogs Season 3 brings an urban map, Limited Mode, and a 185,000-account ban wave

Wardogs' Season 3 will launch on 12th November, complete with a new urban map, a new Limited Mode, and a ban wave targeting 185,000 accounts.

Developer Bulkhead confirmed the details earlier this week, revealing plans for a full wipe and progression changes that it hopes will "recapture the shared discovery and sense of achievement that defined" the 100-player tactical shooter when it first launched in Early Access.

The new map will focus on close-quarters fighting, and for a "more level playing field", players can dip into Limited Mode, which offers "an alternative way to experience" the game as it restricts weapons, ammunition, armour, and vehicles.

While the full list of restrictions is still being decided, it currently includes FMJ-only ammunition, a Tier 2 armour cap, and a reduced attack vehicle selection.

"The mode is designed to preserve the feel of early-to-mid-game combat and reduce the advantage offered by more powerful equipment," the team said.

Bulkhead also confirmed seasons are getting longer. From now on, they’ll last three months, giving players "more time to work towards their goals before each wipe and the development team more time to prepare future updates". Progression will also be "brought closer to the pace of Season 1", following the studio’s acknowledgement that Season 2 accelerated "the journey too aggressively".

"Season 3 is about giving players a new battlefield to learn together and a progression journey worth spending time on," said Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer. "Longer seasons give everyone more room to reach their own goals, and give us the time to properly develop what comes next."

Alongside Season 3, Bulkhead revealed it has used machine learning to review is "activating further layers of its anti-cheat" after analysing 187 million hours of gameplay with help from machine learning. It says having close to four million unique players since launch gave it enough data to pull that work forward from next year.

"[E]xploiters, real-money traders, and gold-farming networks" have been permanently banned and lost their server-hosting privileges, and a player trust score is planned for 2027.

"Protecting the people who play Wardogs fairly is essential to everything we're building," Brammer added.

Bigger changes to the metagame, including a new progression system, are also due in 2027 as Bulkhead works towards Wardogs 1.0. Full Season 3 patch notes will be out before launch.

Wardogs launched in Steam Early Access on 10th September, and is due on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S in 2028.

Wardogs is one of the breakout successes of the year. In our early access Wardogs review, we said the game's mix of competitive shooters' best bits with something entirely of its own made it "a brilliantly refreshing take on the genre".
