#3799. Cartoon-styled "lite-vania" Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh will have you springing yourself, and your summoned pals, from magic jail

Andy Dufresne never thought to use witchcraft, did he

Since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards shows, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.

It looks like this'll be a mix of passively familiar-enhanced punching and more active, mayhaps traditionally Metroid-y power upgrades, Lola's ghastly pals looming over her tiny frame when called upon. It's all presented in a hand-drawn, lightly anime-ish style, complete with a story setup straight out of Saturday morning TV – Lola's only stuck in Skullcatraz because of a summoning-gone-wrong that occurred in pursuit of her school's unlikely Ofsted-compliant 'familiar contest'. I've attended school several times, and will attest that non-sporting contests, which students remain unaware of until seeing a poster for them, do not exist outside of childrens' television*.

This doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

That aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

*Granted, no TV example was ever as egregiously misleading as Jack Black vehicle School of Rock, which convinced me - then a barely-pubescent aspiring bassist - that winning a local Battle of the Bands would pay out thousands in cash, as opposed to the drinks rounds and packs of guitar strings I'd end up competing for a few years later.

The CEO of the publishers behind GTA 6, Take-Two Interactive, isn't quite ready to go on his victory lap just yet, but he is once again enjoying what he thinks might be the most valuable entertainment IP in the world.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the size of of GTA 6's impending launch. In traditional fashion, Zelnick remained pretty humble, telling Rubenstein that "we never claim success before it occurs."

In this instance, he notes, Take-Two and Rockstar have had plenty of success together. "It's true that GTA 5 was a massive hit," he admits. "It sold in over 230 million units, and we believe the Grand Theft Auto franchise as a whole is probably the most valuable intellectual property in the entertainment business, of any type, because of its enormous reach to consumers worldwide."

Zelnick's argument is a potent one, but it's also a little hard to pin down. Off the top of my head, Pokémon and Marvel have certainly generated more money, but that's admittedly off the back of many hundreds more releases (and many more decades, in Marvel's case). Clearly, however, neither of those franchises can match the billions of dollars off a single launch that GTA 6 is set to make next week, or the other billions that the long tail of GTA Online is likely to secure. Pound-for-pound, GTA certainly sends those other heavyweights back to the corner, even if the 13-year gap between releases might be hurting a little.

Despite his quiet confidence in the brand, however, Zelnick is still refusing to count his chickens before they hatch. "The team at Rockstar has been working diligently to try to create something extraordinary with Grand Theft Auto 6," he says. "I believe they will, I'm very optimistic, but as for success, we'll have to wait until November 19 and beyond."

#3797. World of Warcraft: Forever might live officially on PC, but people are playing it on phones and handhelds already

If you're a World of Warcraft: Forever player you're almost certainly having your free time drained as you chain yourself to your desktop PC to play the game, or maybe a laptop. But for a small selection of true enthusiasts, the game is already working on mobile and handheld devices.

One such person showing off WoW: Forever on the go is none other than director of publishing at Larian, Michael Douse, who took to Twitter to show off the MMO being played on an AYN Thor device. For those who don't know, this is a fancy android handheld console, a sort of beefed up DS for the modern handheld aficionado.

"Arguably too many layers of abstraction," writes Douse. In the picture he posted, you can see the player character viewable on the Thor's top screen, while the map, text chat, skill UI, and buffs viewable on the bottom. It looks pretty cool, and is made possible due to JReese702's Github mod you can download at your leisure.

Arguably too many layers of abstraction pic.twitter.com/VjW0IX00Gg

But it's not the only mo-bell at the ball. Another Github WoW: Forever mod, WolkaraForever, gets the game playable on the iPhone Duo. As highlighted by CEO of esports company 100 Thieves Alex Wechsler on Twitter, the game looks to be ported pretty well to the phone, with mobile touchscreen controls viewable on both sides of the screen. Be warned though, as confirmed by Wechsler in a Twitter reply, it'll get your phone running hot.

As a father of 2 kids and always having wanted to play WOW, I’ve finally found a way 🥹 pic.twitter.com/eIVn0gn1WC

This coming alongside World of Warcraft: Forever's built-in (and very good) controller support could mean the game has real potential to spread far and wide across the vast array of different hardware out there. Blizzard has already hinted at plans of porting the game to other platforms, so who knows? Maybe we can expect an official mobile port to tread the path paved by these community-made mods.

#3796. Best Hunter Pets in WoW Forever

A Hunter isn't whole without their Pet, especially in WoW: Forever where Azeroth is a brave new frontier.

The Hunter’s Pet forms a core part of the Hunter experience in World of Warcraft: Forever, with much of their toolkit heavily relying on these partners in combat. In fact, the Hunter has become quite the iconic WoW Class for being able to tame a huge part of the MMO’s bestiary, giving players literally hundreds of options for Pets.

But for those still leveling their Hunters or curious for what other kinds of Pets are awaiting them all over Azeroth, there are indeed some creatures you should tame and fight with in specific situations.

When Forever launched on Nov. 4, Blizzard was quick to roll out a patch two days later (Nov. 6) to strengthen the ability of Hunter’s Pets to become semi-tanks, at least for the Hunters and smaller groups. But on Nov. 10, Blizzard rolled out a quick hotfix that streamlined some things about the Class:

We’re keeping track of how these changes can affect the performance of Pets so far, and we’ll update this list as necessary.

Hunters are DPS characters by nature, and a lot of that damage is usually facilitated by their Pets. And there are just some Pets that stand out among the rest as better damage dealers than their other counterparts. Cats are a standout here, as they’re among the most common Pet Families you can find as you level up.

Some iconic Cats you could aim for would be Broken Tooth (Badlands) and The Rake (Mulgore), but even the Mountain Lions in Hillsbrad can perform well if you’re not gunning for a rare find. Raptors are a close second among recommended damage Pets as they share the same damage mod as the Cat, whereas the Gorilla has a decent AOE and the Scorpid has a stacking Poison.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Hunter’s Pets don’t make good tanks, unlike traditional tanking Classes. With the right Pet Family, a Pet could still provide decent protection to your Hunter while you’re adventuring. Granted, they’re not as strong as we would want a “tanking” Pet to be, but these can take a beating and give a beating of their own.

Boars remain the best first Pets as they stun and give an attack boost to their next hit. If you level up Beast Mastery with the Boar, it might just be a long-term Pet. Meanwhile, Turtles and Crabs have the best defense stats among all Pets.

Say you want to tag along with a party but want to offer something other than having an extra member (your Pet) in tow. Then try to bring any one of these Pet Families in your dungeoning or leveling session. The idea here is that they’re not solely focused on dealing damage, but rather supporting the team in some capacity.

In this case, bring a Wolf to bolster everyone’s melee attack power. But if you feel you already have enough buffs, then a Carrion Bird to lower the enemy’s attack or a Tallstrider to lower the enemy’s armor could be more practical options.

Contrary to popular belief, the Hunter’s Pet should not focus on tanking in PvP, but rather on some form of control. The ideal PvP Pet should usually fit your current target at the moment, or if you’re unequipped to deal with a particular threat that you feel your Pet could help with.

Spiders usually win, as the 4-second rooting can be debilitating for most rotations and setups. If you prefer chasing down targets, then Hyenas and Crabs can slow them enough to leave them vulnerable.

There might be situations when you prefer to not really play with a Hunter’s Pet. Maybe you feel they’re just bringing you down, or you prefer the damage numbers when you’re performing solo.

You can perfectly go solo as a Marksmanship Hunter, courtesy of the Lone Wolf Talent. Getting this Talent gives you a 20% boost to all attacks as long as you don’t have an active Pet.

#3795. Conan: The Black Pyramid shoves the titular barbarian into a very Hades-inspired action roguelite with the addition of a few other familiar heroes

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

Conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past."

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

#3794. As Arc Raiders celebrates its first birthday, publisher Nexon reveals the extraction shooter has topped 17 million sales, but revenue is set to decline

Arc Raiders, Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter, has exceeded 17m copies sold, according to publisher Nexon.

Arc Raiders was released at the end of October 2025, so reaching that milestone in a year is nothing to scoff at. According to Nexon's latest earnings report, however, only 1m copies of those 17 were sold in the third quarter - meaning sales have certainly slowed down.

Relatedly, Nexon said it expects Arc Raiders' revenue to decline in the fourth quarter compared to the same period last year - when the game enjoyed its hugely successful launch - and anticipates revenue will be "broadly flat sequentially". Despite this, the company said Arc Raiders' revenue was "within the outlook", naming its Frozen Trail update as a key moment that brought back some lapsed players while introducing new ones.

Indeed, Frozen Trail boosted the game's Steam player count, and reports suggest it also helped Arc Raiders hit a six-month player high across various platforms.

Even with its slowing sales, Arc Raiders remains one of Nexon's most successful titles. The company primarily attributed an overall year-on-year revenue increase, for the nine months ended 30th September, to the game.

Looking ahead, the biggest question hanging over Arc Raiders is whether or not it's going to get a dedicated PvE playlist. Following a successful test earlier this summer, Embark has been coy, and hasn't said whether PvE will return as a permanent feature. Arc Raiders' Chinese version does have a dedicated PvE mode, and executive producer Aleksander Grøndal said he could see both PvP and PvE modes co-existing in the future.

The upcoming Fable reboot is set to launch on February 23, 2027, and with that date growing inexorably closer Xbox has dropped a new gameplay trailer showcasing four minutes of heroic questing across a rather grim-looking slice of Albion.

The trailer shows off a little bit of everything: some cinematics, some chitchat, the UI, and of course plenty of combat: melee, ranged, and even a bit of magic.

"The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire. Fable 3 may not be everyone's favorite game in the series but it was bright, colorful, exuberant—this video, by comparison, seems downright grim and conventional.

That's about where I land on it: A four-minute clip obviously isn't going to tell the whole story, but with the video being showcased as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary, and the full Fable release now just three months away (unless it's delayed again), it's reasonable to assume that Playground and Xbox would want to put their best foot forward. And, well, this is fine, but I can't say it has me all charged up to play Fable: To me, it just feels kind of flat.

#3792. How to raid other players in ROB RUN

ROB RUN has many ways for you to expand your criminal empire, and raiding other players is certainly a good strategy. While the method isn’t as easy as breaking into NPC houses, you can master the art by following some simple tips.

First, you need to obtain Breach Decoders.

The first task is to get the Decoders, and there are different ways to get them. Uncommon Decoders are the easiest ones to get, and you can obtain them from cabinets, safes, and different containers. You can also find some from the Season 1 battle pass.

If you want to have the Epic Decoder, you can obtain it by exchanging the Uncommon variant. Go to Lenny’s Motel, and you’ll find a barter trader who will provide you with the item for $10,000.

When you’re about to raid a player base, you’ll need to have multiple Decoders. Unlike a house, a player base is a lot more complex when it comes to completing a breach. Each part requires a separate Decoder (or more than one) to gain entry.

In simple words, you’ll need to bring a Decoder for every base part that has a security system.

Completing a raid is pretty simple as long as you have the required Decoders. You have to use them to strip away points from a security terminal until it hits zero. The number of points you have to strip varies across different parts.

While the Fuse slots for a part don’t change, its tier will determine the number of Decoders you’ll need to open them.

Grace Ashcroft, the freshly minted protagonist of Resident Evil Requiem, has all the makings of a great video game scream queen. She overcomes immense adversity even while suffering a severe anxiety condition and she's the new face of one of the most iconic franchises in horror gaming. Capcom has yet to outright confirm she'll return in future Resident Evil games, but the actor who portrays her seems to think she will.

Grace actor Angela Sant'Albano recently took home the Golden Joystick Award for Best Lead Performer, and with Resident Evil Requiem having won Ultimate Game of the Year, it was a big night for the actor. We caught up with her during the event, and she shared her hopes for the future of Grace Ashcroft.

"I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano tells us. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily." Sant'Albano says she's developed a close friendship with Emily actor Emma Rose, and she wants to see Grace take on "a more maternal role and see how she carries that forward."

Throughout the absolute nightmare that Grace endures through Resident Evil Requiem, she evolves from a state of anxiety-induced paralysis to having just enough confidence to shakily defend herself with a gun, and Sant'Albano is looking forward to seeing her reach her full potential, even if she'll never be an action hero like Leon Kennedy.

"I don't think she'll ever be a Leon character. She's never going to be badass, you know, doing roundhouse kicks," she says. "But I do think her courage and her self-esteem will grow the more that she trusts herself and forgives herself for a lot of the things that I think tie her down. So I think there's a long way to go with her."

Resident Evil Veronica, a remake of Code Veronica, is the next big Resident Evil game to come after Requiem, and I think it's safe to say we won't see any Grace Ashcroft. Capcom has yet to reveal the next mainline installment, but after Sant'Albano's win at the Golden Joysticks, I think I can speak for Resident Evil fans everywhere when I say she's a fan-favorite to return in later entries.

#3789. Steam now shows average Steam Deck framerates when browsing games, but Valve says it's considering expanding the feature to other hardware

By providing average data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture".

Valve has released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

As per Valve's announcement post, average framerates are now listed in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of a game's store page, but you'll need to click Learn More to see it. Additionally, the feature is only available for games that have been tested for Deck compatibility - those with Verified, Playable, or Unsupported badges - so while it's not a complete list, it still covers thousands of titles.

According to Valve, average framerates are derived from players running the game on their Steam Decks, assuming they've opted in to provide framerate data. And the store widget also includes another helpful addition: a histogram displaying the percentage of data samples. This shows how often a particular framerate has been reported, and is useful in determining if the game's framerate is sporadic, such as due to stutters.

"The current Steam Deck Verified compatibility rating is based on standardised test criteria, but it may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay," Valve explained of the new feature.

"This is especially true around performance - a game with an Unsupported rating due to unstable performance may be considered playable by some customers, and a Verified game may not reach a framerate that some customers prefer to play at. By providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions."

Currently, Steam's framerate data feature only covers performance on Steam Deck, and for a very good reason: Valve's handheld has standardised hardware, so the results will be the same for all players. However, Valve says it intends to provide framerate data for more devices in the future, but it's not clear if that's ever going to include desktop PCs, considering the complex nature of their hardware configurations.

#3788. Xbox CEO celebrates company’s 25 years on social media but can’t stop herself from hinting at further downsizing and AI usage

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

Happy birthday, Xbox! Here’s to 25 years of human-made entertainment, and 25 more with way fewer developers and way more generative AI.

That’s what CEO Asha Sharma seems to be insinuating with her words today in a reflection on 25 years of Xbox, of which she has been a part for less than one. And yet, her impact has been tremendous, with a massive overhaul this year in her “reset” involving the layoffs of thousands of workers to get the business profitable again.

And it sounds like even more layoffs are to come. We already know that, but the number could be bigger, judging by the tone of her social media post where she champions new technology that we haven’t even begun to feel the full effects of.

“Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command,” Sharma said. “That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars.”

How else would a “a single person” or “a small team” build games that normally take hundreds of people besides cutting costs and using generative AI technology in the stead of those who made games before? And where will those hundreds of people go when they are no longer needed? To the unemployment line, of course!

“While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically,” she said. “As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.”

Sharma said she believes “the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays.” Take from all of this what you will, but what I’m taking from it is she’s saying, in many words, “we will be using AI tools and replacing people with them, so get used to it.” React accordingly.

#3787. Rockstar kills any hopes of streaming GTA 6 from Xbox to PC, but you can stream it to your old Xbox One if you like

Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S. And as part of the same announcement, the developer revealed a key detail about the game's cloud streaming options.

GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming. However, this is only possible on Xbox Series X/S consoles, as well as - surprisingly - the last generation console, Xbox One. Notably, that means you can't use Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream to PC, or other devices, despite it being useable there.

You may recall that in early October, a Verge report said Microsoft had acquired exclusive cloud streaming rights for GTA 6, with the understanding being that the game would be available to stream on any XCloud-supported device - as in, to PC as well. Xbox immediately shot down the report, saying GTA 6 "will not be streaming exclusively or to PC".

Perhaps more surprisingly, the cloud-streamed version will be using Series S graphics settings, not those of the more powerful Series X console. Considering the loss in quality inherent in cloud streaming, this will make for a less-than-ideal way of experiencing the game.

Beyond cloud streaming, GTA 6 supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox, so you can stream the game on your local network to any device, from a PS5 or Xbox Series X/S console.

GTA 6 pre-loading is now available across PlayStation and Xbox. The code-in-box physical editions have also started shipping, letting you claim the code and pre-load your copy in time for GTA 6's 19th November launch.

#3786. Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's important because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history."

Perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

#3785. 60 FPS Zelda or 30 FPS GTA 6, that is the question

30 FPS in 2026, Absolute Cinema or actual Grand Theft?

GTA 6 will be targeting 30 FPS on consoles, per the crucial intel that Rockstar only released far into the most successful preorder campaign ever. Nintendo, on the other hand, stole everyone’s hearts with Ocarina of Time’s 60 FPS version. Will this impact how we see GTA 6?

Rockstar was already $1 billion deep in preorder gold when it revealed that GTA 6 would run at the same framerate that GTA 5 ran at back in 2012. In truth, that was expected, because if it was going to run at 60 FPS, the studio certainly would’ve mentioned it at some point, but this is the kind of news that will always disappoint people who aren’t constantly looking for GTA updates. How much of a dealbreaker could this be? The answer is complex.

I think a good example is that of Bloodborne, a game that barely keeps 30 FPS for one second, but it’s still one of my favorite games of all time. Why? Because it’s that good, and because it was made under the assumption that the team likely wouldn’t get it to run at 60 frames per second on PS4 hardware.

As for GTA 5, most people would’ve preferred it to run at 60 fps even back then, but fans just knew the game would be pushing the PS3 and Xbox 360’s hardware—yes, GTA 5 originally released on those systems—to the limit, so everyone just felt very glad they were even getting something that looked so amazing. Also, GTA 5 pulled off some nice frame pacing, which means that the game didn’t often dip below the targeted mark, and its stability almost made it feel like it was running at a higher framerate than it actually was.

I think players will end up accepting GTA 6’s framerate, because even though a higher count has become much more common these days, GTA 6 is likely going to achieve a solid 30 FPS, which is very different from “targeting” it.

But there’s a possible obstacle on Rockstar’s path: the recently released Ocarina of Time Remake. It runs at a beautifully nimble 60 FPS and is selling so well that there surely will be a lot of overlap between player bases, and that might very well start the 30 vs 60 debate again.

Sure, the games have very different gameplay styles and scope. Still, many gamers need to turn everything into a competition, and Zelda is running on considerably weaker hardware. Nintendo could’ve probably gotten away with Ocarina of Time running at 30 frames per second, because the original ran at under 20. To get Ocarina of Time to run any worse than that, you’ll need the hacked Sega 32X port.

We would always eat up all that sweet Ocarina music regardless of the speed Nintendo played it at, but the company still found us deserving of that extra silky-smooth experience. With all that, those who are all about smooth over cinematic will inevitably question why Rockstar didn’t tone down the graphical fidelity a bit to give us more fluid gameplay for consoles that cost upwards of $800.

And while I can’t tell you exactly why Rockstar made that choice, I remember that running at 60fps was the biggest selling point for GTA 5‘s PC port, so Rockstar might just be going for a tried-and-true sales strategy. Either way, I believe most people will truly enjoy GTA 6 as it comes out, but I’m 100% sure people will only go absolutely nuts for it once it reaches the PC and its sky-high framerate ceilings.

GTA 6 will come out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, and might release on PC earlier than you expect.

Earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed on Twitter that she'd seen The Elder Scrolls 6. Now, she's announcing that MachineGames is making Wolfenstein 3 with a photo of the script attached to a tweet. I don't miss E3, but it feels like a step down in terms of spectacle to go from on-stage trailer reveals to an executive just tweeting it out.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvhNovember 12, 2026

MachineGames followed up a few minutes later with their own tweet, saying, "His reputation precedes him. Wolfenstein 3 is in production." As well as the same photo of the script, they attached a photo of Debra Wilson (who played Resistance cell leader Grace Walker in The New Colossus) recording motion-capture.

It's been a couple of years since Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, though MachineGames did release a Quake expansion for its 30th anniversary in the meantime. A page of script and a photo of a motion-capture session doesn't tell us much about how far along it is, but I wouldn't expect it super soon. It'd be nice to have something to tie into the upcoming Wolfenstein TV series coming from the same folks as the Fallout show.

In a follow-up message, Bethesda confirmed that along with Wilson returning as Walker, Brian Bloom will also be back in the role of series lead BJ Blazkowicz.

What do we think they'll subtitle Wolfenstein 3? MachineGames has an opportunity to really mess with our Steam libraries by calling it "Wolfenstein 3D".

#3783. Cover your robot body in magical fungus aplenty and galavant across a mystical, Soulslike world in MycoRelic, now out in 1.0

Robot, robot, robot, robot, mushroom! Mushroom!

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

#3782. Europe is about to get very tough on loot boxes in games, according to a leaked draft of the landmark Digital Fairness Act

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences..."

An alleged draft of the potentially game-changing Digital Fairness Act has leaked ahead of its scheduled publication tomorrow (11th November), containing proposals that could dramatically affect the way games operate and are monetised within the European Union.

The draft, published by French publication Contexte (via Video Games Industry Memo) goes as far as to recommend that loot boxes (uncertainty-based rewards) be turned off by default for minors, as well as the sale of in-game items and currencies. There's also a recommendation that all players - not just minors - should be able to turn off offers related to these lootboxes and gambling mechanics.

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences," the draft of the Digital Fairness Act begins. "It has enabled faster, more convenient and wider access to an ever-increasing range of goods and services. At the same time, it has given rise to new and more sophisticated ways of influencing consumers' choices.

"Along with the indisputable benefits in choice and efficiency, the extensive use of digital technologies allows both old and new unfair commercial practices to affect consumers at scale, exacerbating risks to their economic interests, as well as to their mental and physical wellbeing. Vulnerable consumers are particularly affected."

The Digital Fairness Act calls for greater transparency around a "transactional decision". Which means: "Price transparency on the real value of in-app purchases using virtual currencies and the probabilities of winning for virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards (loot boxes).

"All consumers can turn off virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards. Some spending-maximising practices prohibited for minors, with the remaining turned off by default. Supporting self-regulation for video games and legal obligation for video games to have an age-appropriate rating. All consumers can turn off attention-maximising features, with some prohibited for minors and the remaining turned off by default."

"Spending-maximising" refers to systems that pressure us to spend more money than we want to, such as reward systems or pay-to-progress or pay-to-win systems. They're all being targeted here, as is virtual currency, which provides a layer of abstraction as to the real cost of goods.

"It may be difficult for minors to resist such perceived pressure to pay," the Digital Fairness Act said with regard to progression-linked systems. "Therefore, where a product is directed at minors or when the trader is aware with reasonable certainty that the product is used by minors, pay-to-progress or pay-to-win mechanisms [...] should not be made available to minors."

The Digital Fairness Act is a forthcoming European legislative proposal designed to update consumer protection rules for various digital dangers that we face today. Importantly, it's not law yet, and it has iterations and discussions to go through before it will be. A timeline on the Digital Fairness Act explainer website suggests it could be adopted late in 2027, then applied more broadly by 2030.

It's also hoping to tackle many things besides shady video game monetisation, including "problematic" influencer marketing, "unfair" pricing practices - such as obscuring the real cost of something until you've progressed through layers trying to buy it - and mysterious-sounding "dark patterns". These relate to 'easy to sign-up, hard-to-cancel' processes, it seems.

These changes aren't happening in a vacuum. Earlier this year, the well-known European age-rating body PEGI announced historic alterations to its game-rating criteria, with an eye to better categorising the dangers of loot box-containing games and aggressively monetised games. These changes have already started to roll out and mean that a game like EA Sports FC, which was previously routinely rated PEGI 3, now automatically gets a PEGI 16 rating because of its Ultimate Team card pack (loot box) system.

The effect of the Digital Fairness Act could tip the balance against these systems being included in games at all. Expect more discussion and digestion of the proposed changes as the Act is officially published tomorrow.

Netflix has announced that Planeswalker, an animated series based on Magic: The Gathering, will debut in 2027. The first sneak peek doesn't show much, but it does suggest that the show is taking several pages from the streamer's wildly popular League of Legends series, Arcane.

The series "chronicles the fierce clash between formidable mages known as Planeswalkers. At the center of this struggle for power and survival burns Chandra, a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts and haunted by her past," according to the official synopsis.

"Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds."

The video above is filled with concept and previsualization clips, but there are a few seconds of what appears to be near-final animation and, well, it's tough to deny a clear Arcane influence here in the character design and animation style. The series is being created by animation studio Digic Pictures, which has previously made cutscenes for games including Assassin's Creed Shadows and Call of Duty: Vanguard, and led several episodes of Amazon's Secret Level series.

Terry Matalas, who served as showrunner for VisionQuest and seasons 2 and 3 of Star Trek: Picard, will be showrunner for Planeswalker. Cindy Appel, who wrote episodes for both those shows, serves as co-showrunner. Patrick Osborne is supervising director and executive producer.

Netflix has been trying to get a Magic: The Gathering series underway since at least 2019, when the streamer announced that the Russo brothers were attached to the project. Whatever vision they had for the series seemingly fell through, as it was five years before we heard about it again – this time, led by Matalas.

In the meantime, check out our guides to the best shows on Netflix and the best movies on Netflix to find out what you should be streaming today.

#3780. All Treasure Rooms in Queen’s Domain and how to find them

Queen’s Domain has five Treasure Rooms, and locating them can be a difficult task. These secret areas are challenging to find, but they offer valuable rewards. In this guide, I will make things easy for you to find all five of them.

Before we can venture to find the treasure vaults, the first task is to get the Keystones. You will need them to open the vaults. Once you reach Obmuer Temple, you can find the first Keystone.

Make your way through the water until you reach a point where a broken structure slopes upwards. Go past it and use the edge to air dash to move forward. You’ll come across a small plot of land where you find one of Aganmi’s missing raiders.

From there, you’ll find an opening in the temple to your right. Drop, and then turn left to find the dark cave. Continue straight, and you’ll find a ledge that drops into a large room with pillars. Go to the other side of the room, enter the open vault, and you’ll find a skeleton sitting with a note next to it.

Read this note to get the Blood Keystone from the shop for 24 Ancient Coins.

There are two Blood Treasure Rooms, and you can find the first one in the basement of the Tower of Knowledge. Once you defeat the boss, clear the growths. This allows you to access a room filled with candle crawlers.

Clear out the enemies, and you’ll discover the door to the Blood Vault. Inside, you’ll get the Rusted Greatsword.

To find the next Blood Vault, head to Verdant Hollow. Go through the Petrified Garden and walk out of the gate that connects the Rotting Cavern and Verdant Hollow.

You can do so using the elevator from the Verdant Hollow wing altar. Walk into the cave from the ledge, and you’ll find the dark room.

Head to Neasied to find the first Velvet Treasure Room. You will find a cave on one side of the area that has the altar on the cliff face. Enter the cave and go all the way down to find a hole. This hole will lead you to another room. Follow the path, and you will eventually reach the elevator that takes you all the way down. You will find the treasure room entrance at this location.

To find the next one, head to the Rotting Cavern. Look for a shine-like structure and follow the path that leads you to it. Eventually, you will come across a sealed door that requires four dark triangular slit pieces. You can find these pieces around the area, and I believe their locations are random. Once you find them, they will lead you to the vault.

There is only one Jade Treasure Room, and you will find it in the Deimpo Mausoleum. Go to the wing altar and take the door on the right. This will lead you to a giant stairwell, and as you descend, you will find the door to the vault.

#3779. Rockstar details Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Pro enhancements, but it'll still only run at 30FPS

Pushing consoles to "their absolute limits".

As Grand Theft Auto 6 preloads go live, developer Rockstar has detailed the enhancements coming to the PS5 Pro version of the game, confirming these won't include framerates above the 30 FPS its targeting for consoles.

Rockstar shared the news in a blog post released to announce that GTA 6 pre-loading is now available ahead of its release date on 19th November.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles," Rockstar says. It goes on to reconfirm GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on all consoles, saying the game is pushing modern machines "to their absolute limits" in order to "bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

PS5 players can expect high-fidelity haptic feedback through the DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio, and Tempest 3D audio, while PS5 Pro enhancements come in the form of PSSR support and ray tracing shadows, which should make the game look especially fancy, plus improved load times. PlayStation players can also expect remote play support. As for the Xbox, the post clarified details on Xbox Cloud Gaming, which will allow the game to be streamed to Xbox consoles including the Xbox One. Notably, this won't work on PC.

Grand Theft Auto 6's 30 FPS target was previously confirmed by Rockstar back in August, but there was some uncertainty around a possible 60fps performance mode at the time. Still, those PS5 technical boons do a lot of work to improve the games it's applied to, which if nothing else should mean GTA 6 will be quite the looker.

Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. Welcome to the new era, folks, where we increasingly seem to be heading closer to a daily coin flip over whether our core online services stay live or go down. This time, it's Microsoft. Down Detector reports problems with Microsoft 365 services since about 12:30 pm (ET) yesterday, November 12, and issues are still ongoing.

Countries across the world are affected, and some institutions have been affected severely. Parts of the UK government, for instance, are having problems sending and receiving emails. The UK's health service, the NHS, has reportedly said it is unable to access online consultation for patients. The US and other governments have reportedly been impacted, too.

Microsoft explains that certain features of services "that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted." So, it looks like Exchange Online could be the culprit. This is the back-end of Microsoft services that use calendars, tasks, emails, and so on.

Affected services include MS365 admin center, apps, Education features, Copilot, Defender for Office 365, Defender XDR, Fabric, Graph, Intune, Planner, Power Apps, Purview, some elements of Teams, To Do, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

In other words, a very extensive list. It's also a list that a bunch of institutions and companies rely on to manage their day-to-day, thus why this is such a big deal.

The latest update from Microsoft, at the time of writing, explains:

"Recovery actions are ongoing and have progressed in phases across affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Global telemetry and customer reports show incremental improvement in several workloads; however, service health remains variable and capacity has not yet fully returned to baseline.

"Network and traffic-management actions remain active. To protect email during recovery, we’re continuing to prioritize queue and backlog processing, and the email timeout window has been extended to 48 hours to preserve delayed messages.

"At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete."

That there is "no evidence of malicious activity" as the cause is promising, but it doesn't stop this from being a severe event that's causing a ton of problems in a ton of countries.

This is the big risk of relying on a single kind of service for all your important online dealings. We saw the same risk bear fruit last year with a global AWS outage that took out a load of online services for a while, and recently we saw similarly widespread issues as a result of PHP vulnerabilities.

We're seeing more and more as time goes on that services from big, usually-reliable companies aren't immune to catastrophe. Let's hope Microsoft figures this one out ASAP.

5. Best high-performance: Lenovo Legion Pro 7i Gen 10

Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born. Eventually, he gave up the ruthless mercenary life to join the world's #1 PC Gaming site full-time. It's definitely not an ego thing, he assures us.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Somehow, some way, the PS5 has been an extraordinary sales success despite launching in the middle of a global pandemic that caused massive supply chain issues and continuing on today amidst an unprecedented memory shortage and economic headwinds driving hardware prices sky high. Despite it all, people are buying PS5s, and many of them.

Sony confirmed just this week that PS5 has hit an incredible milestone of 100 million units sold in its six years on the market. That's not quite as fast as the PS2 or PS4, but it's a much more impressive achievement when you consider one crucial difference between the current-gen PlayStation and literally every other generation before it. Typically, games consoles decrease in price throughout their life cycles, but because of the disadvantages outlined above, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive, right alongside its competitors, the Xbox Series X/S and Nintendo Switch 2.

So, even though the PS5 failed to hit 100 million units sold faster than its predecessors, it still reached the record for units sold without any sort of permanent price cut from Sony. And before you head to the comments section to point out that you got a PS5 at a discount for Black Friday one year, we're talking about official, permanent price decreases from Sony, not temporary sales from retailers. That is seriously impressive considering the economic difficulties not only Sony and other hardware manufacturers are grappling with today, but consumers as well.

You could almost, almost make the case for PS5 being the first console period to hit that sales milestone without a price cut, but for the mighty Nintendo Switch. The Switch hit 100 million units sold in December 2021, and Nintendo never lowered its price globally. There was a price cut in Europe in September 2021, notably just before the Switch reached 100 million units, but it doesn't feel fair disqualifying it from claiming Sony's title for a small, regional price decrease alone.

#3774. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

UPDATE: And the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store history.

UPDATE 11TH NOVEMBER: Grand Theft Auto 6 has also become the most pre-ordered game "of all time" on the Xbox Store, Microsoft has announced. And on that platform, again, the advice is to pre-load because of "unprecedented demand" for the game, a post on Xbox Wire said.

The Xbox difference is that you can use Xbox Cloud to stream GTA 6 to other Xbox devices, although not PC, notably - the game isn't available on PC and presumably Rockstar doesn't want it playable there by any means. Microsoft's stream-deal with Rockstar has also expanded to include Red Dead Redemption 2 "and more", which will be available to stream in the "coming months".

ORIGINAL STORY 10TH NOVEMBER: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

#3773. Wolfenstein 3 and new id Software game confirmed, as Xbox boss somehow unrelatedly shouts about one person soon wielding "capabilities that once required entire nations"

Asha Sharma had a normal one as Xbox turned 25

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#3772. All boss locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Around the Fortnite Treasure Hunters island, there are quite a few bosses you can find and take on in battle, with new ones arriving on a fairly consistent basis. Various quests challenge you to seek out these foes and take them out in battle, which means you need to know where they spawn.

Tracking down any specific character around the island is tough, even on a mini-sized island like the one present in Treasure Hunters, as there’s lots of ground to explore and plenty of spots they could be hiding. If you’re having trouble tracking them all down, here are all boss locations in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

As of the time of writing, there are three bosses you can find around the Fortnite Treasure Hunters island. All of them offer a special weapon from the loot pool, alongside some basic drops like ammo and healing items. Here’s a full breakdown of all key details for each one.

Additional bosses may arrive on the island as the mini-season progresses, as there are big weekly updates with loads of new content. If any others are introduced, we’ll add them here.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

The A$AP Rocky boss only ever spawns at The $.$. Rocky location. This key POI is situated near the middle eastern section of the island. At this spot, you can find him wandering around slightly north of the boat, standing on the beachy area nearby.

You can find the Lil Uzi Vert boss hanging around Lil’ Uzi’s Stronghold. This location can be found near the upper northeast corner of the island. He wanders around the area packed with buildings at this spot, so he can be a bit tough to pinpoint.

Buggy spawns at Buggy’s Beachhead, which was previously known as Loot Lagoon prior to his arrival. You can find this POI near the northern middle section of the island. He spawns outside of the large, shark-themed boat parked at this location.

If you visit any of the boss spawn spots and don’t see them there, this means another player found and defeated them first. Each boss can only be fought once per round, so to ensure you don’t miss out on one of these battles, it’s a good idea to head for one of the boss spawn locations straight out of the battle bus.

#3771. Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!"

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

#3770. Marvel Rivals The Acts of Kurt Wagner event guide

Decipher the prophecies to stop catastrophes.

Nightcrawler has finally made his way into Marvel Rivals, and he’s brought with him a fresh event to tackle. The Acts of Kurt Wagner event has been added to the event page with plenty of rewards you can unlock by progressing through it.

Every Marvel Rivals event is unique, with various special mechanics to navigate and lots of exclusive rewards tied to each one. To help you fully work through this one, here’s a complete walkthrough for The Acts of Kurt Wagner event in Marvel Rivals.

To successfully complete The Acts of Kurt Wagner event in Marvel Rivals, you need to work through a total of four event phases, with eight sections to tackle across all of them. Each part of the event comes with two parts: the Prophecy section, which has three missions, and the Disaster Relief portion, which features another three quests that unlock after you check off the Prophecy part.

All tasks tied to this event task you with completing specific objectives while playing in Quick Match, Competitive, Arcade, or Practice vs. AI. The nature of each specific mission varies, but generally includes relatively straightforward goals like dealing a specific amount of damage, landing a certain number of final hits, and completing a required number of matches.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

To unlock additional missions so you can progress through The Acts of Kurt Wagner event, you first need to complete all available unlocked objectives. All tasks in this event unlock progressively, which means you must work through each individual section to gain access to the next part.

Some parts of this event are locked behind a timer, which means even if you get everything done leading up to it, you’ll have to wait for it to be added. All sections that are locked for a specific amount of time have a countdown on them to help you keep track of this.

There are four exclusive rewards you can earn by progressing through The Acts of Kurt Wagner event. You also get to claim two key currencies for checking off missions throughout it. Here’s a breakdown of all prizes.

The Acts of Kurt Wagner event is available to complete from Nov. 13, 2026 to Jan. 15, 2027. This means you have about two months to work through it and claim all available rewards.

Progressing through this event is a great way to check off key tasks that earn you Chrono Tokens to buy season 11 battle pass skins. There are also lots of other events running alongside The Acts of Kurt Wagner, so if you haven’t completed them all, it’s a good idea to get started on them next. This includes the Night of Illusions event, Path to Doomsday: Avengers Endgame, and Path to Doomsday: Avengers Infinity War.

Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall!

Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach.

Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November:

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review.

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review.

Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review. It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then.

The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review.

We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review. "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote.

There's plenty to be getting on with, then.

Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company after he admitted to an affair on Sunday, and allegations of a second affair came out on Wednesday. Now there are reports of a potential third. Though CTO Colette Kress has taken over in the interim, Nvidia seems to be shopping around for its next CEO, much to the dismay of some Nvidia staff, according to a report from Wired.

It's claimed that a longtime engineer at Nvidia took to an internal suggestion box this week to ask the Nvidia board to consider the company's employees before deciding whether or not to get rid of Huang. This note was made prior to his resignation.

However, over 1,600 comments have been left regarding this suggestion, the majority of which are apparently supportive of Huang. One says, "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss."

Another claims, "We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance."

Notably, not all employees took to the suggestion box to air the same sentiment. One sent an email to the entire company saying, “I stand by Jensen. Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”

That email continues, “If America fails the man who helped build its future, then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”

Jensen Huang's role in Nvidia can't be overstated. As the co-founder of the company, and President and CEO since 1993, he has no doubt been instrumental in its success. And business has been booming for the graphics card company-turned-AI company over the last few years.

No one knows how the Congress investigation will end up, but it's certainly not a great look for an active CEO to be questioned about this either way.

As for who the next Nvidia CEO will be, many names have been floated, from Nvidia staff like CTO Michael Kagan all the way to AMD, Intel, or Arm's current CEOs. President Donald Trump even wishes for Tim Cook, the ex-CEO of Apple, to take Huang's place.

#3767. Microsoft suffer system outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, exec says there's "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity"

Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

That latest update was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of issues.

"We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity."

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there currently looks to have been no big hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

#3765. PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away

After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff.

According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.

"Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities".

Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue.

Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely. Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December.

The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026, following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond.

Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles, Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release.

Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May, but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.
