Dancing with the Stars is a wildly popular reality competition show, which puts out big numbers on ABC (and streaming with a Disney+ subscription). While fans are reeling from the most recent episode that saw Tatyana Ali stay and Jenna Dewan surprisingly eliminated, a contestant from last season is speaking out. Namely Boy Meets World icon Danielle Fishel, who shared that she thinks both the judges and the audience judge women more harshly than the male dancers.

I'm watching DWTS for the first time this season, and the most recent elimination proved to me how important the fan votes truly are. In a clip from the podcast Chicks in the Office's Twitter, Fishel spoke about her experience in Season 34. During it, she got honest about the bias she thinks exists for celebrity contestants, offering:

When I was on the show I didn't want to talk too much about how I felt that the women are maybe more harshly criticized. Not only by the judging, but also by the audience.

While I'm relatively new to Dancing with the Stars, I can see what she's saying. For instance, earlier this season Jena Dewan got middling scores despite being a professional dancer. Then there was #liftgate, where judge Carrie Ann Inaba famously criticized Jenna Johnson's choreography, resulting in her husband Val posting a controversial response and getting suspended for a week. I've also felt like Tatyana Ali and Maura Higgins have both gotten harsher scores than they deserved throughout the current season.

Given the importance of the fan votes, any time the judges get down on one contestant, it has the potential to really sway the public. Later in the same clip, Fishel addressed the way she felt like sometimes the judges pile on contestants, and suggested a way she thinks they could make it better. In the actress's words:

Maybe just pick and choose. Like 'If you're gonna tell her she should articulate her arms, I'm gonna say something really positive.' Just to balance it out a little bit.

As Danielle Fishel said, she kept these thoughts to herself while competing on Season 34 last year. Now she feels comfortable opening up, especially as she watches the current season as a fan. The hosts of Chicks in the Office seem to agree with her, going so far as to say that the judges "treat the grown men on the show like they are children." Clearly, the fanbase is passionate about DWTS, including alumni from the competition series. For her part, Fishel was eliminated 7th last season, which is how far Tyler Cameron and Jackson Olson made it this year.

New episodes of Dancing with the Stars air Tuesdays on ABC as part of the 2026 TV schedule. After hearing Danielle Fishel's comments, I'm definitely going to be paying closer attention to the judging moving forward.

#3736. Don't expect more information on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel "for some time," Bethesda says

After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

#3735. Viva Las Vegas, baby: Rainbow Six reportedly set to return to its high-rolling heights

Call up your buddies, set aside some cash, and get ready to leave it all at the craps tables: Rainbow Six is reportedly heading back to Vegas, baby, Vegas.

According to Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson, three new projects are now in the works at Ubisoft Montreal, and one of them is a new release in the Rainbow Six: Vegas franchise, which last had an entry way back in 2008.

Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six: Vegas launched in 2006 on PC, PS3, Xbox 360, and even the PSP, and Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six: Vegas 2 followed two years later. In the years since, Ubisoft has launched Rainbow Six Siege and its spin-off Rainbow Six Extraction, along with several mobile games, the re-launch of Rainbow Six Siege X, and next year’s turn-based Rainbow Six Tactics.

Henderson says it’s currently unclear what the game will be, but sources state the new project codenamed “Spades” is “likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake, but only time will tell.” Even still, I think a remastered Vegas or Vegas 2 would be cause for excitement in some areas of the internet. He also said one of the other two games at Ubisoft Montreal is another title in the Rainbow universe, so Ubisoft seems to be doubling down and betting big on Rainbow.

The Vegas games followed the Rainbow team dispatched into Las Vegas, Nevada to battle terrorists, featuring a singleplayer campaign and competitive multiplayer that ended up on Major League Gaming’s Pro Circuit.

A return to the Vegas strip would likely be welcome news to many fans, as the Vegas games are regarded by many to be some of the best tactical FPS shooters from their era. I have a friend who I know will be particularly excited, as he was an avid Vegas player who tried to get me to join many times way back when.

A couple of days ago I reported that Reddit is rolling out reviews for different products, informed by Redditors' thoughts and molded by AI into into dedicated review pages for these products. Given Reddit says "many reviews also include images, prices, and purchase links", I wondered whether Reddit would be making any affiliate money from this. In an email sent to me, a Reddit rep explains: "Reddit Reviews is an organic experience, and Reddit does not receive a cut of any purchases made through the buy it now button on product pages."

Not that I would have had a massive problem with this—PC Gamer earns affiliate revenue itself—but I suppose it's good to know there won't be a financial incentive there at least in that respect. And it does at least tie in with the aimed "organic" nature of Reddit in general.

I was also concerned that users might review-bomb products they don't like, or that companies could use bots to positively influence reviews for their own products. Reddit reassures us about that, too:

"Platform-wide, we are taking numerous steps to prevent and enforce against inauthentic content."

That's certainly more reassuring than nothing, but we'll have to see how it goes in practice. AI and bot farms make the modern landscape tricky business, and I'm sure there must already be actors out there giving pretty convincing supposedly first-personal reviews of products on different platforms, whether to bolster or undermine these products.

#3732. Destroy All Humans remake developer goes independent, splits from THQ Nordic and parent company Embracer Group

Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.

The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler said in a press release.

Black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the company swallowed up countless big names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

It doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has said it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Big Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

I didn’t think there was any way Survivor 51 could outcrazy that wild Tribal Council confrontation between Kilby, Lewis, Sharonda, Eric, Cristian and Linnea a few weeks ago where two extra votes were played and they all threatened to draw rocks. Wrong. I was wrong. Last night’s Double Duos twist may have outcrazied that mess, as we got an idol play, two shots in the dark and maybe the weirdest extra vote decision in the history of Survivor. It’s that last part I’m particularly fascinated by, as I’ve watched the episode twice and am still baffled by the decision-making. I’m not the only one either.

Let’s walk through this step by step because there’s a lot going on here. Cristian was picked to go on the journey and earned an extra vote that was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. With all the chaos and uncertainty at Tribal Council, however, he and Carter, who were paired as a duo, decided Cristian should play his shot in the dark to try and earn safety for the pair. If you play your shot in the dark on Survivor, which gives you a 1 in 6 chance of drawing a scroll that keeps you safe, you lose your ability to vote. That meant Cristian couldn’t use the extra vote himself and needed to give it away to someone else.

Cristian has a lot of close allies and is a member of the so-called Salt Alliance, but for unclear reasons, he decided to give the vote to Eric, who is not part of the alliance, during Tribal Council. Now, you might be thinking this is the baffling Tribal Council decision I referenced in the headline, but it’s not. I think it was a weird move, but I sort of understand where Cristian was coming from. He told Eric he was giving him the vote to build trust, and since they do have some history together on a shared pre-merge tribe, he may have thought that was the best way to ensure Eric would vote with them. Personally, I would have just had Carter play the vote, but I can kind of, sort of see where he was coming from.

No, the baffling decision was what Eric then did with that vote. He just put it in his pocket and noped out, despite the fact that he knew it was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. In his voting confessional, he said he didn’t think it needed to be played since he thought they had the numbers on their side. So, he just… didn’t play it and let it expire without ever being used.

I was so confused during my first viewing that I thought I must have misheard the television. Nope. I did not. He just didn’t play it because he thought the votes were already there. Not surprisingly, fans on social media were collectively confused as well. I saw numerous tweets trying to work out the why and even former players calling out his bizarre decision.

Now, to be clear, I’m not saying there’s an obvious play Eric should have made with the extra vote. He could have simply thrown it on Jelly and Dev to solidify that trust with Cristian. He could have thrown a random vote on Mike and Maggie to help protect himself and Thien An in case they caught their own stray vote. Either of those paths would have been perfectly fine, but instead, he did nothing with it and opened himself up to possible problems with Cristian.

Everyone knows how many votes were cast last night. They can all count; so, in theory, Cristian and Carter should be able to figure out that Eric just put the extra vote in his pocket. Maybe they make it a thing. Maybe they don’t. Either way, it seems like a wild gamble to take when the vote has no practical value and at least Cristian and Carter and perhaps more players in that alliance can call him out later if he tries to pretend like it’s a real vote as a leverage move later in the game.

I can’t wait to get a full explanation from Eric whenever he does pregame press about why he didn’t use the extra vote. In a perfect world, we'll even get a confessional about it in the edit next week. Regardless of his reasons though, his decision will go down as yet another example of why this season of Survivor has been the best in a long time, at least so far. The castaways are all over the top and ridiculous. The scheming is incessant, and production has mostly found the right balance between twists and getting out of the way. I can’t wait to see how it all concludes.

#3729. Layoffs, generative AI, and overtime: New study paints bleak picture of 2026 gaming industry

There’s a lot to be excited about in the gaming industry, as new awesome games are constantly being released. But the sad reality is that game development and the industry in general are in a very tough spot.

A new report, GDC’s State of the Game Industry: November 2026, illustrates this unfortunate sentiment and is quite depressing to read through. The top two topics in it are industry layoffs and generative AI, and yeah, that sounds about right when it comes to everybody’s mood inside game dev these days.

Citing people who work in the games industry surveyed from across the world (but mostly the US), GDC also pulled from a pool of 900 laid-off game workers to “dive deeper into their lived experiences.” And here’s the experience: a whopping 68 percent of those laid off from AAA studios were affected in the past year, while 27 percent of them have sent 100 or more job applications since being let go, and 54 percent of them are still unemployed.

And when it comes to sentiment within studios, things are looking and feeling bleak as a result of everything that’s been happening over the past few years, as evidenced by this chart:

A lot of that may have to do with AI usage in the industry, how much it’s being used, and how it’s threatening to take jobs. There’s no good answer for AI in game dev, but most surveyed agree that it should stay in non-creative use only.

But in general, 40 percent of those surveyed say that they use generative AI tools as part of their job, up from 36 percent last year, and 55 percent say that it’s having a negative impact on the industry.

The survey states that “55 percent of game industry professionals think generative AI is having a negative impact on the game industry, unchanged from last year’s 54 percent” and “workers in quality assurance and community support (76 percent) held the most unfavorable views, followed by game design (65 percent), visual and technical arts (65 percent), and audio (57 percent).” Meanwhile, 35% said, “generative AI is having a mixed impact on the game industry, while eight percent said it’s having a positive impact.”

And even with AI, work hours are getting hectic for many: 53 percent said they work over 40 hours weekly, with 13 percent saying they work 51 hours or more, on average, per week.

If you’d like to read the full report, check out the GDC website for all the detailed info.

#3728. Amy Hennig's Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra hasn't been cancelled, Skydance reportedly says, as rumours swirl to the contrary

You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.

Reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku says, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly," Gigliotti reportedly told staff. "There is no truth to these claims."

This follows a recent rumour that the action adventure title was potentially going to get the axe in the near future. The rumour originated from a Marvel 1943 fan account, and while the original X post has since been deleted, it didn't stop it from spreading online, including amongst the game's own development staff.

According to Kotaku's report, Rise of Hydra is close to its alpha state, despite seemingly five years of development. The game is said to have had multiple issues through its long development.

The current build is reportedly "light on gameplay", featuring only one interaction button. This is understood to be the result of Rise of Hydra having reportedly been originally envisioned as a Netflix game. According to the same report, the game is late and over budget, which resulted in cuts to its scope and scale throughout development.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was fully revealed in 2024, and is the debut title of Skydance New Media, the studio headed by veteran designer and writer Amy Hennig, who's famed for her work on the Uncharted series of games.

Though the game was originally planned for release in late 2025, it was later delayed to early 2026 and then again to "beyond early 2026". Earlier this summer, Paramount Games Studio boss Shawn Kittelsen said Rise of Hydra won't be out in 2026, but assured fans it remains in development. According to the report, Rise of Hydra was later delayed to 2027 and beyond.

Tensions are particularly high at the moment following the colossal recent Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, which has already resulted in some job losses at Paramount Games, a group that oversees the game's development, among other projects.

Intel appears to have gained market share from AMD in a rare turnaround for the company. The red team's chips have been in the lead in performance and popularity for many years now, and frankly, they still are. That's what weird about this one: AMD may have lost ground because it makes the best CPUs for gaming.

The latest Q3, 2026 data from market researchers Mercury Research suggests an increase in market share for desktop CPUs of 5.1%. Now, considering AMD has fought tooth and nail for a decade to increase its share to around 35% as of Q2, 2026, dropping down to just 29.9% in the following three months marks a gargantuan lurch back towards Intel.

Our pick for the best gaming CPU is the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and many other AMD chips make up our recommendations. While we do recommend the Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus due to its surprisingly low price tag and plenty of cores, I wouldn't go as far as believing any Arrow Lake chip has been key to turning around Intel's fortunes among gamers. The architecture struggles to keep up with AMD's latest in gaming, and it is built on a dead-end platform—Nova Lake chips are expected soon on a different motherboard socket.

The increase in market share is almost too big to be believed, which is certainly one theory as to what's going on. A rounding error or errant data—though Mercury Research have been pretty locked in in the past. Both Intel and AMD cite their numbers when it makes them look good.

Mercury Research put its hands up to say it isn't totally sure what happened, either:

"It's difficult to know the driver of this for sure, but we speculate that due to the lower mobile CPU demand, Intel could allocate more products to the desktop market, which normally sees a significant demand increase in the third quarter, and Intel had been under-supplying this market earlier in 2026.

"AMD, however, did not appear to have a seasonal increase, which resulted in Intel having a very large sequential and on-year gain in desktop CPU market share," Mercury Research says.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The other theory presented by the market research company is that AMD has "greater exposure" to gaming—by way of offering the best gaming chips.

"We believe another component to Intel's gains here is AMD's greater exposure to the PC gaming market, which has suffered due to supply constraints of gaming GPUs."

Mercury Research say 'supply constraints' when it's more like prices are so absurd for GPUs, RAM, and storage as to be comical, which lends to a general malaise among gamers to building a new PC. But, either way, this theory makes some sense. Intel still holds huge sway with system builders and OEMs, the likes of which are buying up both new and old (DDR4-compatible) chips for cheap systems. And not just gaming systems, which we see both Intel and AMD get a fairly decent share of during our weekly trawling for gaming PC deals.

AMD also admitted it is has a supply deficit at the moment; demand is outstripping supply. It's working to close that deficit, but what it means by that is grow its datacentre chip business more in the coming months and years. After all, AMD is a datacentre company now.

I wouldn't mistake Intel 'gaining market share' as a healthy sign for the company or the wider industry. Mercury Research suggested desktop CPU volumes had seen a "large drop" in Q2, 2026, and both Intel and AMD are said to have seen more than a 10% drop in shipments for mobile chips in Q3, 2026. They're fighting for scraps in the consumer market.

Intel has seen a momentous share price drop as of late due to weak sale expectations due to a crappy PC market, but AMD is set to beat Intel for total revenue by the end of year.

#3725. Horde PVP character lock in WoW Forever, explained

Having trouble making a Horde character in PvP lately? You're not alone.

If you’ve been eager to hop into World of Warcraft: Forever, create a Horde character, say “lok’tar ogar!” (victory or death!) after an intense PvP match, you’re going to have to wait. There’s an ongoing faction lock on Horde characters in PvP rulesets until further notice.

In a game like WoW, premised on being big on faction warfare, achieving some form of balance across player numbers ensures no one side dominates PvP. And since Forever does have a dedicated mega-realm (ruleset) for PvP players, this faction lock has become a source of frustration.

We’ll look into what we know so far, and update you once it’s finally been lifted.

The faction lock happens when you try to switch over to the PvP ruleset and create a Horde character. Chances are, you’ll be stopped by the game. The error box will state this is due to a “population imbalance.”

If you’ve ever encountered faction restrictions in WoW before, this is a similar situation. Just like the error says, it’s very likely that one faction probably had a lot more players than the other.

“While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be,” community manager Kaivax said in a post. “Our goal is to bring things as close to a 50/50 faction balance as possible.”

There is no definitive fix for the faction lock as of writing. Some common (albeit unproven) solutions include the following:

There has been no proof that paying for a new account or getting an account boost can fix the lock, so better to stay safe and avoid these. If you want to wait a couple of minutes, avoid using an auto-clicker to be on the safe side.

While waiting, you could also do the following:

Perhaps the most common “answer” to the lock problem is to create a character in the other faction to help balance the population. Unfortunately, this will lock your account’s PvP ruleset to that faction.

If you already have a character in the PvE ruleset, you can hop on there and enjoy its more casual leveling experience. You can still toggle World PvP via the options menu.

Should you want to take the game’s adventuring fantasy more seriously, maybe the RP-PvP ruleset works for you. This just has the added requirement of actually roleplaying your character, so speaking in dialogue, following cues for anything out-of-character, and just fully immersing in Azeroth. Perfect if you want to roleplay your character’s heritage on top of high-stakes PvP.

Character creation restrictions in PvP rulesets weren’t just exclusive to the Horde, however. Blizzard also locked the creation of Alliance characters to some degree, in a bid to ensure character populations across each faction are as balanced as realistically possible.

As such, you might have some difficulty creating characters of a specific faction in a specific region:

Kaivax assured this is temporary and helps the “long-term health of the ruleset,” especially now when guilds are slowly being established.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Other players took to other avenues to explore the faction lock situation as well. While there’s no definite solution aside from waiting, here are other things you should take into account:

There are also other players who have already experienced some version of faction locking before it got widespread. They also posted about it in the Blizzard forums.

However, Yryadorne from customer service clarified that their team isn’t able to unlock this manually.

Some players asked whether trial accounts also affected the count. These are accounts where you could only play for free until Level 20 (with restrictions) without a subscription. Kaivax replied that their testing concluded the trial accounts had nothing to do with the imbalance. They explained that the 55/45 split focused on the “active logged-in population” of players across all levels.

There’s no evidence that creating a lot of trial accounts would fix the faction balance, especially if part of the consideration is that they are “actively” logged in.

Just to be on the safe side, it might be a good idea to check if your Horde lock is related ot any other character creation errors. Blizzard outlined this list, which could be a useful reference:

A lot of players expressed frustration with the inability to create characters in their favored Faction, especially those who want to sink their teeth into PvP in Forever.

The situation has been particularly difficult for players who also want to play with friends of one faction, only to find out it’s currently locked.

One Blizzard forum post even requested some form of compensation, as there’s no proper communication surrounding the faction lock. Other threads also called out the lack of any virtual queue, estimated waiting time, or any way of knowing how long until the restriction is lifted.

The idea of faction-locking isn’t new to Forever, but it certainly came as a shocker to players still getting used to the idea of having one mega-realm to play on.

Things were different in the OG release and Classic, where you could have characters in different realms. Back then, you could only be Horde on one PvP realm and Alliance on another. Faction rules only applied to new players when one faction was starting to crowd a specific realm, so newcomers had to adjust by joining the rival group.

I'm starting to think Simu Liu really wants another shot at hosting Saturday Night Live. With the sketch comedy series back on the 2026 TV schedule, the Shang-Chi actor has been having a little fun with the show on social media lately, and now he's practically volunteering to impersonate a famous businessman caught up in a very public scandal. Avengers: Doomsday is right around the corner, I'm all for giving him another evening at Studio 8H.

When he hosted SNL in November 2021, the action movie star was a natural, creating some truly unforgettable sketches. So he knows a thing or two about being funny in front of a live studio audience. Liu took to Threads on Tuesday, Nov. 10, with a joke about the ongoing controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. He wrote:

Finally a famous person embroiled in scandal that i can play on SNL.

The tech executive recently admitted to having an extramarital affair amid reports involving a possible foreign intelligence operation. Naturally, the internet has been having a field day with the story, and Liu apparently sees an opportunity for a sketch.

I'm sorry, but somebody has to make this happen. The Barbie standout didn't actually name Huang in his post, but the timing certainly suggests who he has in mind. Given the actor's history of making fun of himself, I can already imagine him walking onstage in one of Huang's signature leather jackets.

For some context, Huang issued a public apology on Nov. 8, acknowledging that he'd been unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia's board also launched an investigation into reports that the CEO may have been targeted by foreign intelligence operatives. The company has said it has no reason to believe its trade secrets or national security were compromised, and those allegations remain under investigation.

It's certainly the kind of complicated, headline-grabbing situation SNL loves to turn into a sketch. Plus Liu already knows his way around the show's particular brand of humor.

When he hosted in November 2021, one of the funniest sketches featured him and Bowen Yang competing over increasingly ridiculous awards for being the first Asian person to accomplish something. The bit poked fun at Hollywood's obsession with representation milestones, and the two played off each other beautifully.

I know Yang has retired from the show, but I'd love to see them reunite for another sketch, especially considering Liu's apparent interest in the Huang story. So someone get Yang on the phone as well, get him involved somehow!

This isn't even his first SNL-related joke this week. As we recently covered, Liu trolled Shane Gillis while showing off his Marvel workout. The actor posted a shirtless gym video using audio from Inde Navarrette's recent SNL monologue, in which she responded to Gillis' controversial comments about women's gym attire.

The MCU star captioned the video, "time to put on my little outfit," which is a pretty funny way to show off all that superhero training while getting involved in an ongoing comedy controversy. At this point, he's practically writing his own audition tape.

Of course, Liu hasn't been announced as one of the show's upcoming hosts, but the timing of his recent jokes couldn't be better. He's reprising Shang-Chi in Avengers: Doomsday, which arrives in theaters Dec. 18, and he's already been having some fun promoting the massive Marvel crossover, including jokingly calling it a little indie movie. So if these posts are his way of getting Lorne Michaels' attention ahead of the premiere, I'm all for it. Give the man another shot at Studio 8H.

Liu has been pretty vocal about wanting to return as Shang-Chi, including recently discussing why Marvel needs to do a better job of making his long-awaited sequel. With Doomsday finally bringing him back into the MCU, another SNL appearance would make a lot of sense.

To be clear, no one has announced that Liu is returning to host SNL. His recent posts could simply be another example of the actor entertaining himself online. But if this is his way of getting the show's attention before Doomsday, I fully support the campaign.

#3722. Will a Grand Theft Auto game ever be set outside of America? Rockstar offers a small glimmer of hope

The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

This is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when company co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and New York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

Nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

While discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij said. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it."

GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

#3721. How does tanking work in WoW Forever?

Being a tank in WoW: Forever can be serious business. Let's get it right.

Tanks in World of Warcraft: Forever form the bastion of every adventuring party. In front of every DPS who sneaks in a hit and healers who keep everyone alive is a tank who takes on the biggest threats. And unlike other games where getting in front of an enemy is enough, some of WoW‘s toughest dungeons need tanks who focus on both the enemy and their allies.

And finding a tank who knows their way around can be difficult. But if you’re a hopeful adventurer who wants to take their step into tankhood, we’ll walk you through the basics. So grab your shield, prep your auras, and let’s pull mobs.

Threat is the most important term in any tank’s vocabulary, since every other tanking concept stems from it. “Threat” is something you generate that determines how likely an NPC is to get aggressive towards you. When an enemy starts attacking you, you’ve generated enough Threat for them to get aggro (aggressive).

No in-game setting reveals how much threat someone generates, and we’ve often had to rely on add-ons (we’ll get to that later) to determine that number. Based on Classic data, Threat usually works like this:

Tanks who attack first secure the Threat. But other party members can easily bypass your Threat level if their damage and heals are absurdly high, usually from DPS and healers. So tanks have to “steal” that Threat back through special abilities. This is where tanks come in with Taunts.

These are abilities that bypass current Threat levels entirely, so NPCs who are affected are forced to attack the caster (tank) instead. Most Taunts last a short while, so tanks usually start rotations with them or whenever tanks feel they need to yoink attention back from mobs. All tanking Classes have Taunts or some other way of stealing aggro back.

Tanks share common qualities even in MMOs. More often than not, they’re the bulkiest units of any party. They’re built to hold the front line, take punishment, and give the rest of the team enough time to finish the fight.

These principles still apply when building a tank in Forever, and these stats are also your ideal targets when pursuing gear in dungeons or crafting them through Professions:

The only stats where these differ would be based on your chosen tanking Class, as some of them have additional stats you should take note of.

The big tl;dr for tanks is to rush to a mob, attack all of them, and use Taunts to keep them away from the party. But that’s just the beginning. Your tank must maintain this momentum regardless of what happens on the battlefield, and these techniques help you adjust to the most common situations:

The ideal scenario in any dungeon is to go to a cluster of mobs, pull them from their general location, and kill them. If you’re with an experienced group, they’d tell you to go to maybe three mob spots at once, pull all of them, and let the team handle it. Both scenarios are correct, but ideally you’d want to take it slow.

Pings are in the game for a reason. Mark your priority target with a skull and a secondary one with a cross. That ensures everyone knows who you plan to focus on stealing Threat from, and they can attack accordingly. Normally, you’d want to target spellcasters first.

When you rush to the mob and start attacking, try not to have your party behind you. Instead, move slowly so the mob follows your general direction until their backs are on the rest of your party. Keep on Taunting throughout the process, so even if Rogues dish out enough DPS to steal Threat, you can force their attention on you. This also ensures your party isn’t being harassed by some stray mob.

As a tank, you likely have spells and abilities that help you absorb damage or resist attacks. Don’t use those buffs all at once. Find rotations where there’s a balance of proccing buffs, attacking mobs, refreshing buffs, and doing it again. If you have instant blocks, save them for critical moments or incorporate them in your rotations.

Your DPS have crowd control abilities to “control” the flow of enemies, and you should take advantage of that. When your damage-dealers stun or slow opponents (Mages with sheep, Rogues with sap, Hunters with traps), try to damage the non-controlled mobs first. Then alternate.

Healers have it tough, as they can generate so much Threat even when they’re not attacking. As a tank, your main priority is to keep the healer alive, since they keep everyone else alive. Ideally, you’d pause if the healer is out of mana so they can recover. A great way to know is to turn on power bars in your party so you can track their resources.

Besides healers, DPS can get ridiculously squishy as their damage numbers can get off the charts. Now a DPS isn’t as useful to the party if they end up soloing mobs or a boss with no one to give backup. Remind your DPS to stay behind mobs at all times, or pull mobs in such a way that they’re facing away from the DPS. Make it a habit to mark your targets, so everyone knows where to focus their attack and who you’re stealing Threat from.

Tanking in WoW: Forever is usually reserved for a select number of Classes with specs tailored for the role. As tanking relies heavily on defense, the Classes that can reliably tank are often the ones that can handle getting hit, can heal themselves after getting hit, or annoy the enemy enough to always stay aggro’d:

Warriors depend on Rage, which they get from hitting and being hit. Their Protection spec is mostly built for tanking, and they have some of the strongest Threat-stealing abilities in the game. Base Warrior alone gets bonus Threat from Defensive Stance and can steal Threat from single targets (Shield Slam, Sunder Armor), mobs (Taunt), and in emergencies (Mocking Blow, Challenging Shout).

They also have nifty tools in their arsenal, such as an early-game interrupt (Shield Bash) and a damage debuff (Demoralizing Shout), among other attacks that often punish opponents.

Paladins are part magic-users, so they also rely on Mana to cast spells. Their Righteous Fury gets them more Threat as they use their toolkit. And just like other tanks, they have their fair share of taunts for single-target (Holy Strike, Seal of Fury and Judgment), and mobs (Consecration).

However, Paladins set themselves apart for their party-wide buffs that reduce damage (Devotion Aura) and give a 10% overall stat boost (Blessing of Kings). Protection is their main tanking spec, but you can also go for Holy if you want to be a sub-healer.

Druids are perhaps the most versatile Class in Forever due to their many forms, and they still have potent heals even as tanks. Their Bear Form is what gets the most threat, and Druids have many mob-based taunts (Challenging Roar, Growl, Swipe) as well. Feral is their main tanking spec, which grants them a decent single-target taunt (Primal Bite). When transformed, Rage is also their primary resource, and it can facilitate vicious combos.

Aside from tanking, Druids can become competent emergency healers. They have access to an instant-cast heal-over-time (Rejuvenation), an instant heal that is upgradeable to an HoT (Regrowth), and a decent AOE (Wild Growth),

#3720. Over A Third Of Game Developers Have Lost A Job In The Last Two Years, Bleak Report Finds

Over a third of all game developers were laid off over the last two years, claims a sobering report from Game Developers Conference (GDC) about the state of the industry. The report surveyed developers from around the world about a number of hot-button topics, from job losses to AI, to get a picture of the industry as we enter perhaps its most unstable era in recent memory.

In response to a question asking about layoffs over the past 24 months, 34 percent of respondents worldwide said they had lost a job in the games industry. U.S.-based developers were even more likely to be laid off at 39 percent. Itâs a trend thatâs only going up, the report adds, noting an increase every time the question has been asked over the past three years. Even those who are employed are not exactly in stable work: only 50 percent of U.S. respondents are employed full-time (down 9 percent).

Of those who have lost their jobsâroughly 900 respondents according to GDCâsome have faced multiple layoffs in that period. 17 percent of this group were laid off twice, with three percent facing three or more layoffs in a 24-month period. With fewer jobs available, over 54 percent say they have not yet found another job, while it took 15 percent of this group over six months to find new work. The results of those finding a job are mixed, too: nine percent ended up finding work outside games, while four percent started their own studio or company.

It paints a worrisome picture. The wealth of experience these developers possess is now at risk of being lost for good. It also hurts morale, with over half of respondents (51 percent) strongly agreeing to the statement that they were âconcerned about my future in the game industry.â A total of 73 percent of respondents at least slightly disagreed with the statement that they were âhopeful about where the game industry is headed.â

The sentiment across all responses in the survey noted developers held pessimistic feelings about the future of the industry and their own prospects within it. With consolidation and AI rampant, itâs hard to blame them. Speaking of AI, while there is a concern that the tech will replace jobs, its usage across the industry remains far lower than in other tech fields. Questioned on AI usage in their development work, 60 percent stated they do not use it. Older developers tend to use it more than younger developers, with significantly more men than women using the tools (45 percent vs 33 percent). Its usage in both indie and premium games was under one-third, with higher usage only being seen by devs working on free-to-play games (58 percent) and mobile-only games (70 percent).

These results go against the conceptions that AI usage is more common than is often disclosed, with a number of developers noting their company either discourages (11 percent) or entirely prohibits (23 percent) AI usage in any capacity. Those who use it, however, are using it very often, most often daily. Concerns over the middling quality of vibecoded releases often give AI a negative reputation, never mind the ways players are often quick to condemn its use. It doesnât help that 56 percent of people see it as having a negative impact on the industry.

The survey, released as part of GDC’s yearly recap of the industry, also touches on topics of working hours and the impact of work on mental health, all pointing toward an unstable time for the game industry. The instability is leading to less advocacy for improving that working situation as wellâwhile support for unions remains high at 80 percent, because layoffs are so frequent and the difficulty of finding a new job so high, the interest in joining unions has actually fallen. People involved in games still love them, and find immense satisfaction from making and playing them. There just isnât much hope surrounding their future right now.

TSMC, the juggernaut that produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips, has discovered a data leak said to contain over 46,000 employee records, according to Seeking Alpha.

The company made a Form 6-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, stating: "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised."

The company says the info has been verified to match data "stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," although said provider is not named. TSMC says it has informed those impacted by the breach and is providing support, and has also engaged with the cloud service vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to "ascertain the facts and take necessary actions."

Taiwanese outlet United Daily News reports that hackers were allegedly offering the employee records on an underground forum for the princely sum of three bitcoin, in exchange for 6.9 GB worth of private data.

The outlet also says that, "according to information online" (via machine translation), hackers were also selling what appears to be TSMC employee data on other forums, releasing a small sample which is said to contain a vast array of personal details, including national ID numbers, addresses, and banking information.

TSMC has confirmed in its statement that the leaked data is unrelated to the company's operations, or customer-related information.

This isn't the first time TSMC has been in the headlines in relation to cybersecurity. Back in 2023, ransomware outfit LockBit attempted to extort the company for $70 million after a claimed hack.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

TSMC denied it had been directly hacked, revealing in a statement that IT hardware supplier Kinmax Technology had been the victim of a "cybersecurity incident" instead, which "led to the leak of information pertinent to server initial setup and configuration." Kinmax also released a statement at the time confirming the breach.

Being such a large and wealthy company at the heart of the tech supply chain, it's no surprise that hackers are keen to gain any details on TSMC if they can. In both these cases, it seems that TSMC's own systems remained secure, but an outside party may have let the side down.

Regardless, I doubt it's the last major data leak I'll be writing about before 2026 is out. This year has been characterised by cybersecurity incidents left, right and centre, and in this every-more-interconnected world, it seems even some of the most security-conscious companies are far from immune.

#3718. Paradox boss Frederik Wester stepping down after several tumultuous years for the Cities Skylines and Stellaris publisher

Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja taking over role.

Paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the company. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level."

Wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a new studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus."

Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.
